Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 3, verses 3–4:

He mentioned the sending down of the Book as a guide (al-Hadi) and the Criterion (al-Furqan), and the Criterion is the victory that distinguishes between truth and falsehood. The reason victory is paired with guidance is that each of them brings about the distinction (al-furqan) between truth and falsehood. For this reason, Allah, the Exalted, called that by which He gives victory to His believing servants a "criterion" (furqan), as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of the Criterion, the day the two armies met﴾. So He mentioned the two foundations: what He sent down upon His Messenger, and the Day of the Criterion, which is the Day of Badr, the day on which Allah, the Exalted, distinguished between truth and falsehood by granting victory to His Messenger and to His religion, and by humiliating His enemies and bringing them to disgrace.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 3, verse 6:**

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "With your Lord there is no night or day. The light of the heavens and the earth is from the light of His Face. The measure of a day of your days with Him is twelve hours. Your deeds of yesterday are presented to Him at the beginning of today's daytime, and He looks at them for three hours. He becomes aware of what He dislikes, and this angers Him. The first to know of His anger are the bearers of the Throne (hamalat al-'arsh), who find it weighing heavily upon them. So the bearers of the Throne, the canopies of the Throne, the angels brought near, and all the other angels glorify Him, until Jibril blows into the horn, and nothing remains but that it hears, and they glorify the Most Merciful for three hours, until the Most Merciful is filled with mercy. That makes six hours."

He said: "Then the wombs are brought, and He looks at them for three hours. This is the meaning of His saying, ﴿It is He who shapes you in the wombs however He wills﴾, and His saying, ﴿He grants to whom He wills females, and grants to whom He wills males, or pairs them, males and females, and makes whom He wills barren﴾. That makes nine hours. Then the provisions are brought, and He looks at them for three hours. This is the meaning of His saying, ﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾, and His saying, ﴿Every day He is upon some matter﴾." He said: "This is your affair and the affair of your Lord."

Narrated by Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani in al-Sunnah, 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi, Shaykh al-Islam al-Ansari, Ibn Mandah, Ibn Khuzaymah, and others.

[Taking the Text Out of Its Apparent Meaning so as to Agree with the Mufti's School]

It is not permissible to take the texts out of their apparent meaning so that they agree with the school of the mufti.

The fifty-fifth benefit: When he is asked about the tafsir (exegesis) of a verse from the Book of Allah or from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he may not take it out of its apparent meaning through corrupt interpretations in order to agree with his sect and his desires. Whoever does this deserves to be barred from issuing fatwas and to have his authority restricted. What we have mentioned is what the imams of Islam, past and present, have expressly stated.

Abu Hatim al-Razi said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i said to me: "The foundation is the Qur'an or the Sunnah. If neither is present, then analogy (qiyas) based on them. When a hadith is traced back to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and its chain is sound, then it is the final authority. Consensus (ijma') is greater than a single report (khabar al-fard). The hadith is taken in its apparent meaning. If it admits of several meanings, then the one that most resembles its apparent meaning is the most preferable. If hadiths conflict in weight, then the one with the soundest chain is preferred. A broken chain (munqati') is not regarded as anything, except the broken chain of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. One principle is not analogized to another principle, and one does not ask a principle 'Why?' or 'How?' Only the branch (far') is asked 'Why?' When its analogy to the principle is sound, it is valid and establishes proof." Narrated by al-Asamm from Ibn Abi Hatim.

Abu al-Ma'ali al-Juwayni said in al-Risala al-Nizamiyya fi al-Arkan al-Islamiyya: "The leading imams of the earlier generations (al-salaf) held to abstaining from ta'wil (interpretation), leaving the apparent meanings as they are and entrusting their true meanings to the Lord, exalted is He. What we approve of as an opinion, and what we hold as our religion, is adherence to the way of the earlier generations of this community. Following is preferable, and abandoning innovation (bid'ah). The decisive textual proof for this is that the consensus of the community is an authoritative proof to be followed, and it is the basis of most of the Shari'ah. The Companions of the Messenger (ﷺ), may Allah be pleased with them, were content to leave aside probing their meanings and seeking what lies within them. They are the elite of Islam and bore the burdens of the Shari'ah alone. They spared no effort in preserving the foundations of the religion, charging one another to preserve them, and teaching people what they needed of it. Had the interpretation of these apparent texts been permissible or obligatory, their concern with them would have surpassed their concern with the branches of the Shari'ah. Since their age and the age of the Successors (tabi'un) passed while they turned away from interpretation, this is conclusive evidence that it is the way to be followed. It is therefore incumbent upon the person of religion to believe in the transcendence of the Creator above the attributes of created beings, not to plunge into interpreting the ambiguous matters, and to leave their meaning to the Lord, exalted is He."

It is recommended, when reciting, to pause at the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7], and then begin with His words: ﴿But those firm in knowledge say: We believe in it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7]. This is a firm practice among the imam of reciters and their master.

Among what is commended from the words of Malik is that he was asked about the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], "How is He established?" He said: "The establishment is known, the modality is unknown, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation." So let the verses of istiwa' (establishment), of coming, and His words: ﴿What I created with My two hands﴾ [Sad: 75], His words: ﴿And there remains the Face of your Lord﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 27], and His words: ﴿Sailing under Our eyes﴾ [Al-Qamar: 14], and what is authentically transmitted from the Messenger, such as the report of the descent, and others, be left as they are, as we have mentioned. End of his words.

Abu Hamid al-Ghazali said: "The correct course for later generations is to follow the path of the earlier generations in unrestricted belief and general affirmation, and in what Allah and His Messenger have said, without inquiry and investigation."

He also said in Kitab al-Tafriqa: "The truth is to follow and to refrain from altering the apparent meaning entirely, and to beware of following interpretations which the Companions did not express, and to close the door of questioning completely, and to restrain from plunging into kalam (speculative theology) and debate." Until he said: "Some people hasten to interpretation on mere conjecture, not certainty. If opening this door and declaring it would lead to confusing the hearts of the common people, then its proponent is to be deemed an innovator. Everything that was not transmitted from the earlier generations as a subject of mention, and that relates to fundamental and important matters of creed of this kind, then it is obligatory to declare as disbelievers those who alter the apparent meanings without a decisive proof."

He also said: "Whatever does not admit of interpretation in itself, and whose transmission is mass-attested (mutawatir), and whose contradiction by any proof cannot be conceived, then contradicting it is pure denial. Whatever admits of the possibility of an interpretation, even by a distant metaphor, then if its proof is decisive, it is obligatory to hold it; if its proof yields only a dominant conjecture and its harm to the religion is not great, then it is an innovation; and if its harm to the religion is great, then it is disbelief."

He said: "The habit of the earlier generations was not to engage in these disputes. Rather, they were severe with whoever plunged into kalam and occupied himself with debate and questioning."

He also said: "Faith derived from kalam is weak. Firm faith is the faith of the common people, which is established in their hearts in childhood through continuous hearing, and after puberty through indications that cannot be expressed."

He said: "Our shaykh Abu al-Ma'ali said: The imam should strive as much as he can to gather the general populace upon following the way of the earlier generations in this matter." End of his words.

The four imams (al-a'immah al-arba'ah) agreed on censuring kalam and its people. The words and position of Imam al-Shafi'i concerning them are well known among all his companions: that they are to be beaten and paraded through their tribes and clans, and it is said: "This is the recompense of whoever abandons the Book and the Sunnah and turns to kalam."

He also said: "I have come to know of the people of kalam something I did not think existed." He said: "For a servant to be tested with everything that is forbidden, short of disbelief, is easier than being tested with kalam." He said to Hafs al-Fard: "I oppose you in everything, even in the words: 'There is no god but Allah.' I say: 'There is no god but Allah, the One who is seen in the Hereafter and who spoke to Moses with direct speech (taklim). And you say: 'There is no god but Allah, the One who is not seen in the Hereafter and does not speak.'"

Al-Bayhaqi said: Al-Shafi'i mentioned Ibrahim ibn Isma'il ibn Ulayyah and said: "I oppose him in everything, and in his words 'There is no god but Allah,' I do not say as he says. I say: 'There is no god but Allah, who spoke to Moses from behind a veil,' while he says: 'There is no god but Allah, who created a speech that Moses heard from behind a veil.'"

He also said at the beginning of the preface to his Risala: "Praise be to Allah, who is as He described Himself, and above what the describers among His creation describe Him." This is an explicit statement that He is not to be described except with what He described Himself, and that He is exalted and far above what the speculative theologians and others describe Him with, which He did not describe Himself with.

Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Sijzi said: I heard my father say: I said to Abu al-Abbas ibn Surayj: "What is tawhid?" He said: "The tawhid of the people of knowledge and the community of Muslims is: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. The tawhid of the people of falsehood is delving into accidents and bodies. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was only sent to deny that."

Some people of knowledge said: How can one not fear lying against Allah and His Messenger, when one bears his words upon far-fetched interpretations and strained metaphors, which are more fit to be riddles and puzzles than clarification and guidance? Can one feel secure that one is among those of whom Allah said: ﴿And woe to you for what you describe﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 18]? Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, it applies to everyone who describes falsely until the Day of Resurrection." And can one feel secure that the words of Allah, exalted is He, do not include him: ﴿And thus We recompense the fabricators﴾ [Al-A'raf: 152]?

Ibn Uyayna said: "It applies to every fabricator of this community until the Day of Resurrection." He, glorified is He, has declared Himself free of everything His creation describes Him with, except the Messengers, for they describe Him only with what He permitted them to describe Him with. He said, exalted is He: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe﴾ [As-Saffat: 180], ﴿And peace be upon the Messengers﴾ [As-Saffat: 181]. And He said: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe, except the chosen servants of Allah﴾ [As-Saffat: 159-160].

It suffices the interpreters that the words of Allah and His Messenger are interpreted with interpretations which they did not intend and which the words of Allah do not indicate. They spoke about Allah according to their own opinions, and put their opinions before the texts of revelation, making them a measure over the words of Allah and His Messenger. Had they known what door of evil they opened upon the community through corrupt interpretations, and what edifice of Islam they demolished with them, and what fortresses and strongholds they plundered, then for any one of them to fall from the sky to the earth would be dearer to him than to engage in any of that.

Every person of falsehood has made the interpretations of previous interpreters an excuse for his own interpretation. He says: "What prohibited interpretation for me and permitted it for you?" Thus the group that denied the Resurrection interpreted the texts about the Resurrection. Their interpretation was of the same kind as the interpretation of those who deny the attributes, indeed stronger than it in several respects known to anyone who weighs the two interpretations against each other. They said: "How are we punished for our interpretation while you are rewarded for yours?" They said: "The texts about the attributes are more manifest and more numerous than their texts about the Resurrection, and their indication is clearer. How then is it permissible to interpret them in a way that contradicts their apparent meaning, while it is not permissible for us to interpret the texts about the Resurrection?"

Likewise the Rafidah (Rafidites) did with the hadiths about the virtues of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and other Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. Likewise the Mu'tazilah did with the interpretation of the hadiths about the vision of Allah and intercession. Likewise the Qadariyyah with the texts about divine decree. Likewise the Harurites and other Khawarij with the texts which contradict their doctrines. Likewise the Qaramitah and the Batiniyyah closed the gate, filled the valley over the wellspring, and interpreted the whole religion. So the root of the ruin of religion and of the world is nothing but the interpretation which Allah and His Messenger did not intend by their speech, and which does not indicate that it is what they meant. Have nations ever disagreed with their prophets except through interpretation? Has any great or small strife occurred in the community except through interpretation? Through its gate it entered, and has the blood of Muslims been shed in strife except through interpretation?

This is not peculiar to the religion of Islam alone. Rather, all the religions of the messengers remained upon uprightness and rectitude until interpretation entered them, and then there entered into them corruption which none knows except the Lord of the servants.

The good tidings of the authenticity of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) have been widely transmitted in the earlier scriptures, but they imposed interpretations upon them and corrupted them, as Allah, glorified is He, informed us of their distortion, alteration, and concealment. Distortion (tahrif) is the distortion of meanings through interpretations which the speaker did not intend. Alteration (tabdil) is the replacement of one word with another. Concealment (kitman) is denying it.

From these three diseases the religions and creeds were changed. If you reflect on the religion of Christ, you will find that the Christians entered into corrupting it through interpretation in a manner hardly found anywhere else among religions, and they entered it through the gate of interpretation.

Likewise the heretics of all nations entered into corrupting the religions of the messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, through interpretation. Through its gate they entered, upon its foundation they built, and upon its points they wrote.

[Motives for Interpretation]

Those who interpret are of many kinds, according to what motivates them to interpret, and according to the weakness or strength of their understanding. The greatest in going to extremes in false interpretation is the one whose intention and understanding are corrupt. The worse his intention and the more limited his understanding, the more deviant his interpretation. Among them is one whose interpretation arises from some kind of desire without any doubt, rather he acts with insight into the truth. Among them is one whose interpretation arises from some kind of doubt that appeared to him and concealed the truth from him [and among them is one whose interpretation arises from some kind of guidance without any doubt, rather he acts with insight into the truth]. Among them is one in whom both come together: desire in intention and doubt in knowledge.

**[Some Effects of Ta'wil (Figurative Interpretation)]**

In sum, the divisions among the People of the Two Books, and the division of this Community into seventy-three sects, were caused only by ta'wil. The blood of the Muslims was spilled at the Battle of the Camel, at Siffin, at al-Harra, in the fitnah of Ibn al-Zubayr, and so on, all through ta'wil. The enemies of Islam, the philosophers (al-mutafalsifah), the Qaramitah, the Batiniyyah, the Isma'iliyyah, and the Nusayriyyah, entered through the gate of ta'wil. Islam has never been afflicted by a trial except that its cause was ta'wil. Its trial comes either from those who interpret (al-muta'awwilun), or from the disbelievers being empowered over Muslims because of what those interpreters committed: they interpreted, opposed the apparent meaning of the revelation, and justified themselves with falsehoods.

What shed the blood of the Banu Jadhimah, when they had embraced Islam, if not ta'wil, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and disavowed before Allah the act of the interpreter who killed them and took their property? What caused the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, to hold back from following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyyah, if not ta'wil, until his anger intensified at their hanging back from obeying him, and they turned back from that ta'wil? What shed the blood of the Commander of the Faithful, 'Uthman, unjustly and aggressively, and brought upon the Community what has befallen it until now, if not ta'wil? What shed the blood of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and his son al-Husayn, and the members of his household, may Allah be pleased with them all, if not ta'wil? What shed the blood of 'Ammar ibn Yasir and his companions, if not ta'wil? What shed the blood of Ibn al-Zubayr, Hujr ibn 'Adi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others of the leaders of the Community, if not ta'wil? What was the cause of the blood of the Arabs being spilled in the fitnah of Abu Muslim, if not ta'wil? What stripped Imam Ahmad between the two punishments and had him whipped until creation cried out to its Lord, the Exalted, if not ta'wil? What killed Imam Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Khuza'i and imprisoned a multitude of scholars until they died in prison, if not ta'wil? What unleashed the swords of the Tatars upon the abode of Islam until they subjugated its people, if not ta'wil? And did the sect of heresy, the people of indwelling (hulul) and unification (ittihad), enter except through the gate of ta'wil?

And has the gate of ta'wil been opened except in opposition to, and contradiction of, the judgment of Allah in His teaching His servants the clear speech (al-bayan), which Allah bestowed upon man as a favor in His Book by teaching it to him? So ta'wil by riddles, puzzles, and sophistries is more deserving of being rejected than clarification and explanation. Has anyone distinguished between rejecting the realities that the messengers reported from Allah and commanded, by means of false interpretations opposing them, and rejecting them and refusing to accept them? The former is a rejection of denial and obstinacy, and the latter is a rejection of deception and dissimulation.

Abu al-Walid ibn Rushd al-Maliki said in his book entitled *al-Kashf 'an Manahij al-Adillah* (Uncovering the Methods of the Proofs), after mentioning ta'wil and the harm it does to the Shari'ah, until he said: ﴿As for those in whose hearts there is deviation, they follow that which is ambiguous of it﴾. These are the people of disputation and kalam (speculative theology). The gravest thing this category has brought upon the Shari'ah is that they interpreted much of what they thought was not on its apparent meaning, and they said: "This interpretation is what is meant by it. Allah commanded it in the form of the ambiguous (mutashabih) as a trial for His servants and a test for them." We seek refuge in Allah from having a bad opinion of Allah. Rather, we say: the Mighty Book of Allah came inimitable only in terms of clarity and explanation. How far from the intent of the Lawgiver is the one who says about what is not ambiguous that it is ambiguous, then interprets that supposed ambiguity according to his own claim, and tells all people: "Your obligation is to believe in this interpretation." Like what they said about the verse of istiwa' (ascension) over the Throne and other matters, of which they claimed the apparent meaning was ambiguous. Then he said: In sum, most of the interpretations that their proponents claimed were the intent of the Shari'ah, when you examine them, you find no proof stands behind them.

**[The Example of the Interpreters]**

Then he said: The example of one who interprets some part of the Shari'ah and claims that his interpretation is what the Shari'ah intended is like someone who comes to a medicine compounded by a skilled physician to preserve the health of all people, or most of them. A man comes, and that great medicine does not suit him because of a bad temperament he has, which only affects a minority of people. So he claims that some of the medicines the first physician named in that widely beneficial remedy did not mean the common medicine by which the name is customarily understood in speech, but meant another medicine that could be indicated by that name through a distant metaphor. He then removes that first medicine from that great compound, puts in its place the medicine he thinks the physician intended, and tells the people: "This is what the first physician intended." People then use that compounded medicine in the way this interpreter interpreted it, and the temperaments of many people are corrupted. Then others come, sense the corruption of people's temperaments from that compounded medicine, and try to correct it by replacing some of its medicines with another medicine different from the first. As a result, a kind of illness afflicts the people that is different from the first kind. Then a third comes and interprets some of the medicines of that compound in a manner different from the first and second interpretations, so a third kind of illness afflicts the people, different from the two preceding kinds. Then a fourth interpreter comes and interprets another medicine different from the earlier medicines, and a fourth kind of illness afflicts the people from it, different from the earlier illnesses. When time lengthened over this great compounded medicine, and people applied ta'wil to its medicines, altered and replaced them, various illnesses afflicted the people, until the benefit intended by that compounded medicine was lost for most people. This is the condition of the sects that arose within this Shari'ah with respect to the Shari'ah. Each sect interpreted something different from what the other sect interpreted, and claimed that it was what the Lawgiver intended, until the Shari'ah was torn into every shred, and moved very far from its original subject.

When the Lawgiver, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and his family, knew that this would occur, and must occur in his Shari'ah, he said ﷺ: "My community will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one." He meant by the one the sect that followed the apparent meaning of the Shari'ah and did not interpret it.

If you reflect on what has befallen this Shari'ah at this time of corruption that has entered it through ta'wil, you will realize that this example is accurate.

The first to alter this great medicine were the Khawarij, then the Mu'tazilah after them, then the Ash'ariyyah, then the Sufis. Then came Abu Hamid, who filled the valley over the villages. This is his statement in its wording.

If we were to set out to cover everything that ta'wil has wrought upon this world and religion, and all the corruption that befell nations, past and present, because of it, that would require several volumes. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 3, verse 14:

As for his placing wealth before children in many verses, this is because children, once wealth exists, are a blessing and a joy, but in poverty and hardship they are a worry and a harm. This is from the category of placing the cause before the effect, since wealth is the cause of the complete blessing of children.

As for His saying: ﴿The love of desires for women and sons is made attractive to people﴾, the placing of women before sons is by way of causation, and the placing of wealth before sons is by way of rank.

(A benefit concerning the placing of sons before wealth)

As for the verse of Ali 'Imran, since it is in the context of reporting what has been made attractive to people of desires, which they have preferred over what is with God and have been satisfied with, it placed first that to which desire is most strongly attached and to which the soul is most eagerly inclined, namely women, whose trial is the greatest of the trials of this world, and who are the fetters that have stood between the servants and their journey to God. Then it mentioned the sons who are born of them. A person desires a woman for pleasure and desires a child, and both are sought by him for their own sake. Then it mentioned the desire for wealth, because it is sought for the sake of something else, so its desire is the desire of means. It placed first its most noble type, which is gold, then silver after it. Then it mentioned the desire attached to livestock, which does not live with people in the companionship of women and children, so the desire attached to it is less than the desire attached to them. It placed first the most noble of this kind, which is horses, for they are the fortresses of a people, their strongholds, their honour and their dignity. It placed them before the grazing animals, which are camels, cattle and sheep. Then it mentioned the grazing animals and placed them before tillage, because beauty and benefit from them are more apparent and greater than from tillage, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home and when you send them out to pasture﴾. Their benefit is greater than that of tillage, for one benefits from them by riding, eating, drinking, clothing, goods, weapons, medicine, and provision, and other aspects of benefit. Also, their owner is more honoured and more noble than the owner of tillage. This is what is observed, for the owner of tillage must inevitably have some kind of humiliation. For this reason one of the early pious predecessors, when he saw a plough, said: "This has not entered the house of a people except that humiliation entered them." Thus he placed tillage at the last of the ranks, placing it in its proper position.

(Section)

Restraint from desire is easier than patience with what desire demands.

For it either demands pain and punishment; or it cuts off a pleasure more complete than it;

or it wastes a time whose waste is regret and remorse;

or it damages a reputation whose preservation is more beneficial to the servant than its damage; or it takes away what its survival is better for him than its loss;

or it lowers a rank and standing whose maintenance is better than its lowering;

or it strips away a blessing whose continuance is more pleasant and sweeter than the fulfilment of desire;

or it opens a path for a lowly person to you which he would not have found before that;

or it brings worry, grief, sorrow and fear which do not approach the pleasure of desire;

or it makes you forget a knowledge whose remembrance is more pleasurable than attaining desire;

or it causes an enemy to rejoice and a friend to grieve;

or it cuts the road upon a blessing that is coming toward you;

or it produces a defect that remains as an attribute that does not pass away, for deeds produce attributes and character traits.

(A benefit)

As for excusing oneself by destiny, it is a contesting with God, a plea by the servant against the Lord, and an attribution of one's sin to the decrees, and this is the act of God's adversaries, as one of their shaykhs said concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The love of desires for women and sons and heaped-up hoards of gold and silver is made attractive to people﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 14]. He said: "Do you know what is meant by this verse?" They said: "What is meant by it?" He said: "Establishing the excuses of creation."

This ignorant person, who is ignorant of God and His speech, has lied. What is meant by it is rather to discourage one from this perishing, passing world, to encourage one toward the lasting, enduring one, and to belittle those who prefer this adorned thing and follow it, by the status of the child who is made to find attractive what he plays with, so he is delighted by it and moves toward it, although the one who makes it attractive is not mentioned; He did not say "we made it attractive to people." God, Exalted is He, attributes the adornment of the world and sins to the devils, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And Satan made their deeds attractive to them﴾ [al-An'am: 43], and He said: ﴿And thus their partners made the killing of their children attractive to many of the polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 137]. And in the hadith: "I was sent as a guide and a caller, and guidance is not in my hands at all; and Iblis was sent as one who misleads and makes attractive, and misguidance is not in his hands at all." And this does not contradict His saying: ﴿Thus We made attractive to every nation their deeds﴾ [al-An'am: 108], for the attribution of the adornment to Him is by decree and destiny, and to Satan is by causation. Moreover, His adornment is a punishment for them for their inclination toward what Satan made attractive to them; so from the punishment of an evil deed is an evil deed after it, and from the reward of a good deed is a good deed after it.

The point is that the plea of destiny is incompatible with repentance, and it is not at all a form of excuse. In some reports: "When the servant commits a sin and says: 'O Lord, this is Your decree, You decreed it upon me, You judged it upon me, You wrote it upon me,' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'You did it, You earned it, You willed it and you strove, and I shall punish you for it. And when he says: "O Lord, I wronged, I erred, I transgressed, I did it," Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "I decreed it upon you, I decided and wrote it, and I forgive you." And when he does a good deed and says: "O Lord, I did it, I gave charity, I prayed, I fed," Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "I helped you, I granted you success." And when he says: "O Lord, You helped me and granted me success, and You bestowed favour upon me," Allah says: "You did it, You willed it, You earned it."'"

So excuse is of two kinds: an excuse that negates acknowledgment, and that is incompatible with repentance; and an excuse that affirms acknowledgment, and that is part of the completeness of repentance.

(Section)

The point is that He, glory be to Him, made wealth and poverty a test and a trial for gratitude, patience, truthfulness and falsehood, sincerity and polytheism. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿That He may test you in what He has given you﴾ and said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tried? And We certainly tried those before them, and God will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars﴾ and said: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with God is a great reward﴾.

So He made the world a fleeting commodity and a deceptive enjoyment, and made the Hereafter the abode of recompense and reward, and surrounded the world with desires and adorned it with them, as He said: ﴿The love of desires for women and sons and heaped-up hoards of gold and silver and branded horses and grazing animals and tillage is made attractive to people. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, and with God is the best return﴾. So He, glory be to Him, informed that this which He adorned the world with of its pleasures and desires, and which is the ultimate aim of the wishes of its seekers and those who prefer it over the Hereafter, is seven things: women, who are the greatest of its adornments and desires and the greatest of its trials; sons, through whom a man's completeness, pride, generosity and honour lie; gold and silver, which are the material of desires in their varied kinds and types; branded horses, which are the honour, pride and fortresses of their owners and the instrument of their domination over their enemies in pursuit and flight; grazing animals, from which come their riding, food, clothing, furnishings, goods and other of their interests; and tillage, which is the material of their sustenance and the sustenance of their animals and beasts, their fruit, their medicines and other things.

Then He, glory be to Him, informed that all of that is the enjoyment of the worldly life. Then He stirred His servants toward the enjoyment of the Hereafter and informed them that it is better than this enjoyment and more lasting, saying: ﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who fear God is with their Lord gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and purified spouses and approval from God." And God is Seeing of the servants﴾.

Then He mentioned who deserves this enjoyment and who its people are, those who are most worthy of it, saying: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire"; the patient, the truthful, the devoutly obedient, the spender, and those who seek forgiveness before dawn﴾. So He informed that what He prepared for His righteous friends of the enjoyment of the Hereafter is better than the enjoyment of the world, and it is of two kinds: a reward they enjoy, and greater than it, which is His approval of them. God said: ﴿Know that the life of this world is but amusement and diversion and adornment and boasting among you and competition in wealth and children, like the example of a rain whose plants please the disbelievers; then it dries up and you see it turned yellow; then it becomes debris﴾. So He informed about the reality of the world by means of what He made visible to people of insight: that it is play and amusement, in which souls take diversion and bodies are occupied. Play and diversion have no reality; they are a distraction to the soul and a waste of time, by which the ignorant are cut off, so it passes away wasted for nothing. Then He informed that it is an adornment made attractive to the eyes and the souls, so the eyes and souls were captivated by it through approval and love. Had the hearts truly known its reality, its outcome and its destination, they would have hated it, and would have preferred the Hereafter over it, and would not have preferred it over the enduring, lasting thing, which is better and more lasting.

The Imam said: "Waki' related to us: al-Mas'udi related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'What have I to do with the world? My likeness and the likeness of the world is that of a rider who rested in the shade of a tree on a summer day, then went on and left it.'"

In the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the world weighed with God the wing of a mosquito, He would not have given a disbeliever a drink of water from it."

Al-Tirmidhi said: a sound hadith.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The world compared with the Hereafter is no more than what one of you puts his finger into the sea, and let him see with what it returns," and he indicated with the index finger.

In al-Tirmidhi, from his hadith, he said: "I was with a group who stood with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) beside a dead young goat, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do you see this, that it was despised by its people until they threw it away?' They said: 'And who would be ...? If they threw it away, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The world is more despised by God than this is by its people.'"

And in al-Tirmidhi also, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The world is cursed, and cursed is what is in it, except the remembrance of Allah and what accompanies it, and a scholar or a student."

Both hadiths are sound (hasan). Imam Ahmad said: Haytham ibn Kharijah related to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar al-Nahrani, who said: 'Isa (peace be upon him) said to the disciples (al-Hawariyyun): "Truly I say to you, the sweetness of this world is the bitterness of the Hereafter, and the bitterness of this world is the sweetness of the Hereafter, and the servants of God are not the ones who live in luxury. Truly I say to you, your worst deed is a scholar who loves the world and prefers it over the Hereafter; if he could, he would make all people in his work like himself."

Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed me, from Makhul, who said: 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said: "O company of disciples, which of you can build a house on the waves of the sea?" They said: "O Spirit of God, who is able to do that?" He said: "Beware of the world, and do not take it as a dwelling place." In the Kitab al-Zuhd of Ahmad: that 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) used to say: "Truly I say to you, eating bread, drinking sweet water, and sleeping on rubbish heaps with dogs is much for one who wishes to inherit Paradise."

In the Musnad, from him: "Allah struck the food of the son of Adam as a parable for the world, and that its... and its salt; let him look at what it becomes."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 3, verse 18 (part 1 of 8):

God invoked those possessed of knowledge (ulu al-ʿilm) as witnesses to the greatest thing to which witness can be borne, which is His Oneness, so He said: ﴿God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those possessed of knowledge, standing firm in justice.﴾

This indicates the virtue of knowledge and of its people in several respects:

The first: that He invoked them rather than other than them among mankind.

The second: that their testimony is joined to His testimony.

The third: that it is joined to the testimony of His angels.

The fourth: that within this is their commendation and vouching for their integrity, for God does not call upon as witnesses from among His creation except the upright (ʿudul). From this is the well-known report from the Prophet: "This knowledge will be carried by the upright of every generation, who will remove from it the distortion of the extremists, the false claims of the falsifiers, and the misinterpretation of the ignorant." (ﷺ)

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yaʿqub ibn Shayba said: I saw a man bring a man before Ismaʿil ibn Ishaq the judge, and he brought a claim against him. He questioned the defendant, who denied it. He said to the claimant: Do you have evidence? He said: Yes, so-and-so and so-and-so. He said: As for so-and-so, he is among my witnesses; as for so-and-so, he is not among my witnesses.

He said: Does the judge know him? He said: Yes. He said: By what means? He said: I know him through books of ḥadīth. He said: How do you know him through his books of ḥadīth? He said: I know nothing but good.

He said: The Prophet said: "This knowledge will be carried by the upright of every generation." So the one whom the Messenger of God has declared upright has more right to be so declared than the one you have declared upright. He said: Stand up and bring him, for his testimony is accepted.

The discussion of this ḥadīth will come, God willing, in its place.

The fifth: that He described them as "those possessed of knowledge" (ulu al-ʿilm), and this indicates their being specially associated with it, that they are its people and its companions, and that this is not a borrowed title for them.

The sixth: that He invoked Himself as witness, which is the greatest witness, then the best of His creation, who are His angels and the scholars among His servants. This suffices them as virtue and honour.

The seventh: that He invoked them as witnesses to the greatest and most mighty thing to be witnessed, which is the testimony that there is no god but God. Those of great rank are only invoked as witness to a great matter by the eminent and noble of creation.

The eighth: that He made their testimony a proof against the deniers, for they stand in the position of His proofs, signs and demonstrations that point to His Oneness.

The ninth: that He used a singular verb for the act of testimony that includes it, issued from Himself, His angels and them, and did not join their testimony to any other act than His own testimony. This indicates the strength of the connection between their testimony and His testimony. It is as though He bore witness to His own Oneness through their tongues, causing them to speak this testimony. So He is the witness to it on His own behalf by establishing, causing to utter and teaching it, and they are the witnesses to it on His behalf by acknowledgment, confession, affirmation and faith.

The tenth: that He made them discharge His right before His servants through this testimony. When they bear it, they have discharged the truth borne witness to, and so the truth borne witness to is established, and it becomes obligatory upon creation to acknowledge it. This is the ultimate of their happiness in this life and the next. Whoever is guided by their testimony and acknowledges this truth because of their testimony, they have a reward like his. This is a great virtue whose extent none knows but God. Likewise, whoever bears witness to it following their testimony, they too have a reward like his. These are ten aspects of this verse.

The eleventh, concerning the virtue of knowledge and its people: He negated equality between its people and others, as He negated equality between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. He said, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ And as He said: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal.﴾ This indicates the utmost of their excellence and nobility.

The twelfth aspect: He made the people of ignorance like the blind who cannot see. He said: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ So there is none but a knower or a blind one. He has described the people of ignorance as deaf, dumb and blind in more than one place in His Book.

The thirteenth aspect: He informed about those possessed of knowledge that they see that what was sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, and He made this a praise of them and an invocation of them as witnesses. He said, exalted is He: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth.﴾

The fourteenth aspect: He commanded asking them and returning to their statements, and made that like testimony from them. He said: ﴿We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the reminder if you do not know.﴾ (7)

The people of the reminder are the people of knowledge of what was sent down to the prophets.

The fifteenth aspect: He bore witness to the people of knowledge with a testimony that includes invoking them as witnesses to the soundness of what God sent down to His Messenger. He said: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, detailed? And those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be of the doubters.﴾ (114)

The sixteenth aspect: He consoled His Prophet through the faith of the people of knowledge in it, and commanded him not to pay heed to the ignorant at all. He said: ﴿And a Qur'an We have divided that you may recite it to the people over a period, and We have sent it down in stages. Say: Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down on their faces in prostration, and say: Glory be to our Lord; the promise of our Lord is indeed fulfilled.﴾ (106–108)

This is a great honour for the people of knowledge, and it implies that its knowing people have recognised it, believed in it and affirmed it, whether or not others believe in it.

The seventeenth aspect: He praised the people of knowledge, extolled them and honoured them by making His Book clear signs in their breasts. This is a special quality and distinction for them over others. He said: ﴿And thus We have sent down to you the Book. Those to whom We have given the Book believe in it, and among these are those who believe in it, and none deny Our signs except the disbelievers. And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you write it with your right hand, for then the falsifiers would have doubted. Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who were given knowledge, and none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers.﴾ (47–49)

Whether the meaning is that the Qur'an is firmly established in the breasts of those given knowledge, preserved and steadfast within them, while being in itself clear signs—in which case it is described with two statements, the first that it is clear signs, and the second that it is preserved, established and steadfast in the breasts of those given knowledge—or the meaning is that it is clear signs in their breasts, that is, its being clear signs is known to them and firm in their breasts, the two views are mutually implicated, not contradictory. Under both readings, it is a praise of them and a commendation, within which is the invoking of them as witnesses. So reflect on this.

The eighteenth aspect: He commanded His Prophet to ask Him for increase in knowledge. He said in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿Exalted be God, the True King. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.﴾ (114)

And it suffices as a noble mark of knowledge that He commanded His Prophet to ask Him for more of it.

The nineteenth aspect: He informed about the elevation of ranks of the people of knowledge and faith in particular. He said in Surah al-Mujadila: ﴿O you who believe, when you are told to make room in assemblies, make room; God will make room for you. And when you are told to rise, rise; God will raise those who believe among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees. And God is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (11)

God, exalted is He, has informed in His Book of the raising of ranks in four places. The first is this one. The second is His saying: ﴿The believers are only those whose hearts feel fear when God is mentioned, and when His signs are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely; who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them. Those are the believers, truly. For them are degrees with their Lord, and forgiveness and noble provision.﴾ The third is His saying: ﴿And whoever comes to Him as a believer who has done righteous deeds, for them are the high degrees.﴾ (75) The fourth is His saying: ﴿And God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and lives over those who sit back by a great reward—degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy.﴾ (95–96)

These are four places. In three of them the elevation in degrees is for the people of faith, which is beneficial knowledge and righteous action. The fourth is elevation through jihad. Thus all elevation in degrees returns to knowledge and jihad, by which the religion is sustained.

The twentieth aspect: He invoked the people of knowledge and faith as witnesses on the Day of Resurrection against the claim of the disbelievers. He said: ﴿And on the day the Hour comes, the criminals will swear they remained not but an hour; thus were they deluded. But those who were given knowledge and faith will say: You have remained within the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not knowing.﴾ (55–56)

The twenty-first aspect: He informed that they are the people of His fear, indeed He restricted them among mankind to this. He said in Surah Fatir: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear God. Indeed, God is Mighty, Forgiving.﴾ This is a restriction of His fear to those possessed of knowledge. And He said: ﴿Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual dwelling beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.﴾ (8)

He has informed that the people of His fear are the scholars, so this indicates that this mentioned reward is for the scholars by the combination of the two texts.

Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, said: Fear of God is sufficient as knowledge, and self-delusion about God is sufficient as ignorance.

The twenty-second aspect: He informed about His parables which He strikes for His servants, to guide them to the soundness of what He has informed, that the people of knowledge are those who benefit from them and are specialised in their knowledge. He said: ﴿And these parables We strike for the people, and none understand them except the knowers.﴾

In the Qur'an there are some forty-odd parables. Some of the early generations, when they passed a parable they did not understand, would weep and say: I am not among the knowers.

The twenty-third aspect: He mentioned the debate of Abraham with his father and his people, and his victory over them by argument, and informed of his preference and the raising of his rank through knowledge of argument. He said, exalted is He, following his debate with his father and people in Surah al-Anʿam: ﴿That was Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise, Knowing.﴾ (83) Zayd ibn Aslam, may God be pleased with him, said: "We raise by degrees whom We will" means by the knowledge of argument.

The twenty-fourth aspect: He informed that He created creation, and placed His Sacred House, the sacred month, the offering and the garlands, so that His servants may know that He is over all things Powerful and that He has encompassed all things in knowledge. He said: ﴿God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth, the like of them. The command descends among them, that you may know that God is over all things competent, and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge.﴾ (12)

This indicates that the servants' knowledge of their Lord, His attributes and His worship alone is the ultimate purpose sought from creation and command.

The twenty-fifth aspect: God, exalted is He, commanded the people of knowledge to rejoice in what He has given them, and informed that it is better than what people accumulate. He said: ﴿Say: By the bounty of God and His mercy—so in that let them rejoice. It is better than what they accumulate.﴾

The bounty of God was interpreted as faith, and His mercy as the Qur'an. Faith and the Qur'an are beneficial knowledge, righteous action and guidance, and the religion of truth, and these two are the best knowledge and the best action.

The twenty-sixth aspect: He bore witness to whomever He gave knowledge that He has given him much good. He said in Surah al-Baqara: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good.﴾ (269)

Ibn Qutayba and the majority said: wisdom is attaining the truth and acting upon it, and it is beneficial knowledge and righteous action.

The twenty-seventh aspect: He enumerated His blessings and favour upon His Messenger, and made among the greatest of them that He gave him the Book and wisdom and taught him what he did not know. He said: ﴿And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom, and taught you what you did not know, and the bounty of God upon you has been ever great.﴾

The twenty-eighth aspect: He mentioned His believing servants with this blessing, commanded them to thank Him for it, and to remember Him for His bestowal upon them. He said: ﴿Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves who recites to you Our verses and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you what you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.﴾ (151–152)

The twenty-ninth aspect: When He informed His angels that He would place a successor on earth, they said to Him: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with Your praise and sanctify You?﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, I know what you do not know.﴾ (30) And He taught Adam the names, all of them, then presented them to the angels and said: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.﴾ (31) They said: ﴿Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise.﴾ (32)

Up to the end of the story of Adam, and the command to the angels to prostrate to Adam, Iblis refused, so He cursed him and expelled him from heaven.

The demonstration of the virtue of knowledge from this story has several aspects:

The first: when the angels asked Him how He would place on earth those who would be more obedient to Him than they, He said: ﴿Indeed, I know what you do not know.﴾

He answered their question by saying that He knows, of the hidden matters and their realities, what they do not know, and He is the Knowing, the Wise. From this it became apparent that among this successor were the best of His creation: His messengers, prophets, righteous servants, martyrs, the truthful, the scholars and the ranks of the people of knowledge and faith, who are better than the angels; and it became apparent that among Iblis were the worst of the worlds. So He brought forth this and that, while the angels had no knowledge of this, nor of that, nor of the wise purposes in the creation of Adam and his settlement on earth.

**Second:** When He, glorified is He, wished to display the preference, distinction and excellence of Adam, He singled him out by knowledge. He taught him all the names, then ﴿presented them to the angels and said, "Tell Me the names of these, if you are truthful."﴾ It is related in the tafsir (exegesis) that they said, "Our Lord will not create a creation more honoured by Him than us." They thought that they were better and more excellent than the vicegerent whom Allah would place on the earth. When He tested them with knowledge of what He had taught this vicegerent, they confessed their incapacity and their ignorance of what they did not know, and they said, ﴿"Glory be to You. We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise."﴾ Then He showed them Adam's excellence through the knowledge with which He had singled him out. He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." When he informed them of their names, they acknowledged his superiority.

**Third:** When He, glorified is He, made them recognise Adam's excellence through knowledge, and their incapacity to know what he had been taught, He said to them, ﴿"Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal?" (33)﴾
Thus He made Himself known to them through the attribute of knowledge, that He encompasses their outward and inward states and the unseen of the heavens and the earth. He made them known to the excellence of His prophet and interlocutor through knowledge, and their incapacity regarding what Adam had been given of knowledge. This alone is sufficient as an honour for knowledge.

**Fourth:** He, glorified is He, placed in Adam attributes of perfection by which he was superior to other created beings. He, glorified is He, wished to show His angels his excellence and nobility, so He displayed to them the best of what was in him, which is his knowledge. This indicates that knowledge is the noblest thing in man, and that his excellence and nobility lie only in knowledge.

A parallel to this is what He did with His prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him). When He wished to display his excellence and nobility over all the people of his time, He showed the king and the people of Egypt, from his knowledge of the interpretation of their dreams, what the scholars of interpretation could not achieve. Then he was advanced, empowered, and entrusted with the treasures of the earth. Previously he had been imprisoned because of the beauty of his face and the comeliness of his appearance. When the beauty of the form of his knowledge and the splendour of his understanding became apparent to them, they released him from prison and established him in the land. This indicates that the form of knowledge is more radiant and beautiful in the sons of Adam than the sensory form, even if that sensory form were the most beautiful.

This is an independent aspect of the preference of knowledge, added to what preceded, and with it the aspects reach thirty.

**The thirty-first aspect:** He, glorified is He, condemned the people of ignorance in many places in His Book. He said, the Exalted, ﴿"But most of them are ignorant."﴾ He said, ﴿"But most of them do not know."﴾ He said, the Exalted, ﴿"Or do you suppose that most of them hear or understand? They are not but like livestock; rather, they are further astray in way." (44)﴾
He did not limit Himself to comparing the ignorant to cattle; He made them more astray than them in way.
He said, ﴿"Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason." (22)﴾
He informed that the ignorant are the worst of living creatures in His sight, across their varieties: donkeys, predators, dogs, insects and all other creatures. The ignorant are therefore worse than them. Nothing is more harmful to the religion of the messengers than the ignorant; rather, in reality they are its enemies. He, the Exalted, said to His prophet, whom He had protected, ﴿"So never be among the ignorant."﴾
His interlocutor Musa (peace be upon him) said, ﴿"I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant."﴾ He said to the first of His messengers, Nuh (peace be upon him), ﴿"I advise you lest you be among the ignorant."﴾
This is the state of the ignorant in His sight, and the former is the state of the people of knowledge in His sight. He also informed of His punishment upon His enemies: that He prevented them from knowing His Book, understanding it and comprehending it. He, the Exalted, said, ﴿"And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed barrier. (45) And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness..." (46)﴾
He commanded His prophet to turn away from them, saying, ﴿"And turn away from the ignorant."﴾ He praised His servants for turning away from them and disengaging from them, as in His saying, ﴿"And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, 'For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace be upon you; we do not seek the ignorant.' (55)"﴾
He, the Exalted, said, ﴿"And when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace.'"﴾ All of this indicates the ugliness of ignorance in His sight and His hatred for ignorance and its people. It is the same among people, for everyone disowns it, even if they themselves have some of it.

**The thirty-second aspect:** Knowledge is life and light, and ignorance is death and darkness. All evil stems from the absence of life and light, and all good stems from light and life. Light reveals the realities of things and clarifies their ranks, and life is what makes the attributes of perfection sound, which necessitate the correctness of words and deeds. Whatever arises from life is entirely good, like modesty (haya'), whose source is the perfection of the life of the heart and its perception of the reality of ugliness and its aversion to it. Its opposite is shamelessness and obscenity, whose source is the death of the heart and its lack of aversion to what is ugly. Likewise, modesty is like rain, by which every thing lives. He, the Exalted, said, ﴿"Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness, never to emerge from it?"﴾
He was dead through the ignorance of his heart, so He gave him life through knowledge and made for him a light of faith by which he walks among the people. He, the Exalted, said, ﴿"O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and make for you a light by which you will walk, and forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. (28) So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty. (29)"﴾
He, the Exalted, said, ﴿"Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into light. And those who disbelieve, their allies are the taghut (false objects of worship); they bring them out from the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever." (257)﴾.

**The thirty-third aspect:** Allah, glorified is He, made the game caught by an ignorant dog forbidden to eat, and permitted the game caught by a trained dog.
This too is from the nobility of knowledge: only the game of a knowledgeable dog is permitted, while the game of an ignorant dog is not lawful to eat. This indicates the nobility and excellence of knowledge. Allah, the Exalted, said in Surat al-Ma'ida, ﴿"They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say, 'Lawful for you are the good things, and what you have taught the hunting animals, training them as you were taught by Allah. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah over it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.' (4)"﴾
Were it not for the distinction of knowledge and teaching and their nobility, the game of a trained dog and of an untrained dog would be equal.

**The thirty-fourth aspect:** Allah, glorified is He, informed us about His chosen one and interlocutor, to whom He wrote the Torah with His own hand and spoke to him, that he travelled to a knowledgeable man in order to learn from him and increase his knowledge beyond his own. He, the Exalted, said, ﴿"And when Musa said to his young man, 'I will not cease until I reach the junction of the two seas, or I will continue for years.' (60)"﴾
Out of his eagerness to meet this scholar and to learn from him, when he met him, he adopted with him the manner of a student with his teacher. He said to him, ﴿"May I follow you on the condition that you teach me of what you have been taught of guidance?"﴾ He began, after greeting, by asking permission to follow him, and that he would not follow him except with his permission. He said, ﴿"On the condition that you teach me of what you have been taught of guidance."﴾
He did not come as one to be tested, nor as one who was already a student; rather, he came as a student seeking more knowledge added to his own. This alone is sufficient as excellence and honour for knowledge. The prophet of Allah and His interlocutor travelled and journeyed until he suffered the weariness of his journey in learning three matters from a knowledgeable man. When he heard of him, he could not rest until he met him and asked him to let him follow him and teach him. In their story there are lessons, signs and wisdoms, but this is not the place to mention them.

**The thirty-fifth aspect:** His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"And it is not for the believers to go forth all together. Why should not a group from every division among them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may be cautious? (122)"﴾
In Surat al-Tawba, the Exalted urged the believers to acquire understanding of the religion, which is learning it, and to warn their people when they return to them, which is teaching. There is disagreement about the verse. It was said that the meaning is that the believers should not all go forth for understanding and learning; rather, from every division a group should go forth to gain understanding, and then return to teach those who remained behind. On this reading the going forth is a going forth for learning, and the word "ṭā'ifa" (group) is used of one person or more. They said: this is evidence for the acceptance of the report of a single narrator (khabar al-wahid). On this view al-Shafi'i and a group of others interpreted it.
Another group said: the meaning is that the believers should not all go forth to jihad; rather, one group should go forth for jihad, and another division should remain behind to gain understanding in the religion. When the group that went forth comes back, those who remained behind instruct them and teach them what has been revealed of the religion, and the lawful and unlawful. On this reading, His saying "that they may gain understanding and that they may warn" refers to the division from which the group went forth. This is the view of the majority. On this reading, the going forth is a going forth for jihad in its original sense, for wherever this word is used, jihad is what is understood from it. Allah, the Exalted, said, ﴿"Go forth, light and heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives."﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "There is no migration after the conquest, but there is jihad and intention; and when you are called to go forth, then go forth."
This is the well-known meaning of this word. On both views, the verse is an encouragement to gain understanding of the religion, to learn it and to teach it, for that is equal to jihad, and may even be better than it, as will be explained in its place, if Allah wills, in the hundred and eighth aspect.

**The thirty-sixth aspect:** His saying, the Exalted, in Surat al-'Asr: ﴿"By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise each other to truth and advise each other to patience. (1-3)"﴾
Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "If all people reflected on this surah, it would suffice them." The explanation of this is that the ranks are four, and by completing them a person attains the ultimate of his perfection:
First: knowing the truth.
Second: acting upon it.
Third: teaching those who do not know it well.
Fourth: patience in learning it, acting upon it, and teaching it.
He, the Exalted, mentioned the four ranks in this surah, and swore by time in this surah that every person is in loss except those who believe and do righteous deeds. These are the ones who knew the truth and affirmed it; this is one rank. ﴿"And do righteous deeds"﴾ refers to those who acted upon the truth they knew; this is another rank. ﴿"And advise each other to truth"﴾ means they enjoined it upon one another in teaching and guidance; this is a third rank. ﴿"And advise each other to patience"﴾ means they were patient upon the truth and enjoined upon one another patience and steadfastness in it; this is a fourth rank. These are the ultimate perfection, for perfection is that a person be perfect in himself and make others perfect. His perfection is through the reform of his two faculties, the cognitive and the practical: the reform of the cognitive faculty is through faith, and the reform of the practical faculty is through doing righteous deeds. Making others perfect is through teaching them, being patient with them, and enjoining patience upon them in knowledge and action. Thus this surah, despite its brevity, is among the most comprehensive surahs of the Qur'an for all good, in its entirety. Praise be to Allah, who made His Book sufficient against everything other than it, a cure for every disease, and a guide to every good.

**The thirty-seventh aspect:** He, glorified is He, mentioned His favour and bounty upon His prophets, messengers, friends and servants through what He gave them of knowledge. He mentioned His blessing upon the seal of His prophets and messengers by His saying, ﴿"And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom, and taught you what you did not know. And ever has the bounty of Allah been upon you magnificent."﴾
This verse has already been mentioned. He said about Yusuf, ﴿"And when he reached his maturity, We gave him judgement and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good."﴾ He said about His interlocutor Musa, ﴿"And when he reached his maturity and was fully grown, We gave him judgement and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good."﴾
Since what Allah gave Musa of this was a great matter, which He singled him out with over others, and which only the strong, the people of resolve (ulu al-'azm), could bear, He prepared it for him after he had reached his maturity and was fully grown, meaning after his strength was complete.
He said about the Messiah, ﴿"O Isa, son of Maryam, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother, when I supported you with the Holy Spirit, you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and when I taught you the Book and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel."﴾
He said about him, ﴿"And He will teach him the Book and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel."﴾ Thus He made his teaching among what He gave good news of to his mother, and comforted her eye with it.
He said about Dawud, ﴿"And We gave him wisdom and decisive speech."﴾
He said about al-Khidr, the companion of Musa and his young man, ﴿"So they found a servant from among Our servants, to whom We had given mercy from Ourselves and taught him knowledge from Our presence."﴾
Thus He mentioned among his favours upon him his teaching and what He gave him of His mercy.
He, the Exalted, said, mentioning His favour upon Dawud and Sulayman, ﴿"When they judged concerning the field, when the sheep of a people grazed in it by night, and We were witness to their judgement. (78) And We gave understanding of it to Sulayman, and to each of them We gave judgement and knowledge... (79)"﴾
He mentioned the two noble prophets and praised them for judgement and knowledge, and He singled out one of them with understanding of the case. I have mentioned the two judgements, the Dawudi and the Sulaymani, their reasoning, who among the imams took this view and who took that, and the preference for the Sulaymani judgement on several grounds, its agreement with analogy and the principles of the Shari'a, in the Book of Ijtihad and Taqlid.
He, the Exalted, said in Surat al-An'am, ﴿"Say, 'Who sent down the Book which Musa brought as a light and guidance for the people, which you make into scrolls, disclosing some and concealing much? And you were taught what neither you nor your fathers knew.' Say, 'Allah...' (91)"﴾
That is, the One who sent it down made their being taught what neither they nor their fathers knew a proof of the validity of prophethood and messengership, since this knowledge is only attained from the side of the messengers. How then could they say, ﴿"Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being"﴾? This is from the excellence and nobility of knowledge, and that it is a proof of the validity of prophethood and messengership. Allah is the granter of success to right guidance. He, the Exalted, said, ﴿"Allah certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though before that they had been in clear error. (164)"﴾

And Allah the Exalted said in Surah al-Jumu'ah:

﴿He it is who raised among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and the wisdom, though before that they were in clear error. (2) And [He raised him] among others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Mighty, the Wise. (3) That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾

He means: and He sent [him] also to others among them who have not yet joined them.

There is a difference of opinion regarding this negated "joining." It was said that it means joining in time, i.e., their time comes after theirs. It was also said that it means joining in merit and precedence. On both interpretations, Allah, glory be to Him, bestowed a favour upon them by teaching them after ignorance and guiding them after misguidance. What a great favour, surpassing all favours, and too exalted for servants to be able to pay its price.

The thirty-eighth aspect: The first surah Allah revealed in His Book was Surah al-Qalam, and in it He mentioned the favour He bestowed upon humankind by teaching them what they did not know. He mentioned His grace in teaching and His preference of humankind through what He taught them, and this indicates the nobility of teaching and knowledge. He, the Exalted, said:

﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created. (1) He created man from a clinging substance. (2) Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous. (3) Who taught by the pen. (4) He taught man that which he did not know. (5)﴾

He opened the surah with the command to read, a reading that arises from knowledge, and He mentioned His creation, both specifically and generally. He said: ﴿Who created, created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.﴾ He singled out man from among creatures because of the marvels and signs He deposited in him, which indicate His lordship, power, knowledge, wisdom, perfect mercy, and that there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him. Here He mentioned the beginning of man's creation as a clinging substance, because the clinging substance is the beginning of the stages through which the drop of semen passes, so it is the starting point of the process of formation. Then He repeated the command to read, informing about Himself that He is the Most Generous (al-Akram). This is the superlative form of generosity (karam), which means abundance of good, and no one is more deserving of this than Him, glory be to Him. All good is in His hands, all good comes from Him, all blessings are from Him who bestows them, and all perfection and glory belong to Him. So He is truly the Most Generous. Then He mentioned His teaching, generally and specifically. He said: ﴿Who taught by the pen.﴾ This includes the teaching of angels and people. Then He mentioned the teaching of man specifically: ﴿He taught man that which he did not know.﴾

These words comprise the fact that He is the giver of all existing things in all their categories, for existence has four levels:

The first is its external reality, indicated by His saying "created."
The second is its mental existence, indicated by His saying: ﴿He taught man that which he did not know.﴾
The third and fourth are the verbal and the written. The written is expressed in His saying: ﴿Who taught by the pen.﴾ The verbal follows necessarily from teaching by the pen, since writing is a branch of speech, and speech is a branch of conception.

So these words encompass all levels of existence, and that He, glory be to Him, is the giver of them through His creation and His teaching. He is the Creator and the Teacher. Everything in external reality came into being by His creation, every knowledge in the mind was attained by His teaching, and every word on the tongue or writing by the finger is by His empowerment, creation, and teaching. This is among the signs of His power and proofs of His wisdom. There is no god but Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. The point is that He, glory be to Him, made Himself known to His servants through what He taught them of writing, speech, and meaning, by His wisdom. So knowledge became one of the proofs indicating Him, indeed among the greatest and most manifest of them. And this is sufficient as nobility and virtue for it.

The thirty-ninth aspect: He, glory be to Him, named the rational proof "authority" (sultan). Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Every sultan in the Qur'an is a proof." This is like His saying:

﴿They said, "Allah has taken a son." Exalted is He; He is the Self-Sufficient. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. You have no authority for this. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ (68)

He means: you have no proof for what you say, and what you say is nothing but speech about Allah without knowledge. And He said:

﴿They are not but names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority.﴾

He means: Allah has not sent down any proof or evidence for them; rather, they are from your own selves and your fathers. And He said:

﴿Or do you have a clear authority? Then bring your book, if you should be truthful.﴾

He means: a clear proof. So bring it, if you are truthful in your claim.

There is one exception where there is disagreement, which is His saying: ﴿My wealth has not availed me; my authority has gone from me.﴾ (69:28-29)

It was said that the intended meaning is power and dominion, i.e., my wealth and kingdom have gone from me, so I have neither wealth nor authority. It was also said that it is in its literal sense, i.e., my proof has been cut off and nullified, so I have no proof.

The point is that Allah, glory be to Him, named the proof of knowledge "authority," because it entails the authority and empowerment of its holder. So he has authority through it over the ignorant. Indeed, the authority of knowledge is greater than the authority of the hand. This is why people submit to a proof in ways they do not submit to force. For hearts submit to proof, whereas it is only the body that submits to the hand. Proof captivates the heart, leads it, and humbles the opponent, even if he displays stubbornness and arrogance; his heart is subdued, humiliated, and overpowered under its authority.
