Moreover, the authority of rank, if it is not accompanied by knowledge by which one governs, is like the authority of beasts of prey and lions and the like: power without knowledge or mercy. This is unlike the authority of proof, which is power with knowledge, mercy, and wisdom. Whoever lacks authority in his knowledge, either his proof and authority are weak, or the authority of the hand and sword has overpowered him. Otherwise, proof is self-sustaining, manifest over falsehood, and dominant over it.

The fortieth aspect: Allah, the Exalted, described the people of the Fire as ignorant and informed that He blocked the paths of knowledge to them. He, the Exalted, said, relating about them:

﴿And they will say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze." (10) So they will acknowledge their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze! (11)﴾

They reported that they used to neither listen nor reason, and hearing and reason are the foundations of knowledge, through which it is attained. And He said:

﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.﴾ (7:179)

So He informed that they did not acquire knowledge through any of the three avenues of knowledge: reason, hearing, and sight. As He said elsewhere: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not reason.﴾ (2:171) And He, the Exalted, said in Surah al-Hajj:

﴿Have they not travelled through the earth so that they might have hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts within the breasts.﴾ (22:46)

And He said:

﴿We made for them hearing, sight, and hearts, but their hearing, their sight, and their hearts availed them nothing, since they used to deny the signs of Allah, and there encompassed them what they used to mock.﴾ (46:26)

Thus He described the people of wretchedness, as you see, by the absence of knowledge. He likened them to livestock at one time, to the donkey that carries books at another, made them more astray than livestock at another, made them the worst of creatures in His sight at another, described them as dead, not living, at another, informed that they are in the darknesses of ignorance and error at another, and informed that over their hearts are coverings, in their ears deafness, and over their eyes a veil. All of this indicates the ugliness of ignorance, the blame of its people, and His hatred for them. Just as He loves the people of knowledge, praises them, and commends them, as has preceded. And Allah is the One sought for help.

The forty-first aspect: What is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whomever Allah wills good for, He grants him understanding in the religion."

This indicates that whoever is not granted understanding in his religion, Allah has not willed good for him, just as whoever Allah wills good for, He grants him understanding in his religion. And whoever is granted understanding in his religion, Allah has willed good for him, if by "understanding" is meant knowledge that entails action. But if by it is meant mere knowledge, then it does not follow that whoever is granted understanding in the religion has had good willed for him, since understanding in that case is a condition for the will of good. On the first reading, it is a cause. And Allah knows best.

(Section)

This noble verse includes the affirmation of the reality of monotheism (tawhid), the refutation of all these sects, and the testimony to the falsehood of their statements and doctrines. This becomes clear only after understanding the verse by explaining what it contains of divine knowledge and realities of faith.

This verse comprises the most noble, the greatest, the most just, and the most truthful testimony, from the most noble witness, concerning the most noble thing witnessed. The expressions of the early scholars regarding "shahida" (He bore witness) revolve around judgment and decree, informing and clarifying, and reporting. Mujahid said: "He judged and decreed." Al-Zajjaj said: "He made clear." A group said: "He informed and reported." All these statements are true, with no contradiction among them, for testimony comprises the speech and report of the witness, his word, and it comprises his informing, reporting, and clarifying. It therefore has four levels. The first level is knowledge, awareness, and belief in the soundness and establishment of what is witnessed. The second is speaking it and articulating it, even if he informs no one else, but speaks it to himself, mentions it, and pronounces or writes it. The third is informing others of what he witnessed, reporting it to them, and clarifying it for them. The fourth is binding them to its content and commanding them to it.

So Allah's testimony to Himself of oneness and of upholding justice comprises these four levels: Allah's knowledge of that, His speaking of it, His informing and reporting it to His creation, and His commanding and binding them to it.

As for the level of knowledge: testimony to the truth necessarily includes it, for otherwise the witness would be testifying to what he has no knowledge of. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Except one who testifies to the truth while they know.﴾ (43:86) The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Upon the likes of this, testify," and he pointed to the sun.

As for the level of speech and report: whoever speaks something and reports it has testified to it, even if he does not utter the word "testimony." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Bring your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this." And if they testify, do not testify with them.﴾ (6:150) And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.﴾ (43:19)

So He made that from them a testimony, even though they did not utter the word of testimony, nor did they render it before others. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The testimony of falsehood is equal to associating partners with Allah." The testimony of falsehood is false speech, as Allah said: ﴿And avoid the statement of falsehood, being true in faith to Allah, not associating others with Him.﴾ (22:30) When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The testimony of falsehood is equal to associating partners with Allah." So he named false speech "testimony." And Allah, the Exalted, named a servant's acknowledgment against himself a testimony. He said: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves.﴾ (4:135) So a person's testimony against himself is his acknowledgment against himself. In the authentic hadith concerning the case of Ma'iz al-Aslami: "When he testified against himself four times, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stoned him." And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They said, "We testify against ourselves." And the worldly life deceived them, and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.﴾ (6:130)

This, and its like in multitude, indicates that a witness before a judge or others is not required, for the acceptance of his testimony, to utter the word of testimony. This is the position of Malik and the people of Medina, and it is the apparent meaning of Ahmad's words. No one from among the Companions or the Successors is known to have required that. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Men whom I approve of testified before me, and the one I approve of most is 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade prayer after the dawn prayer until the sun rises, and after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets." It is well known that they did not utter the word of testimony. And the ten whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) testified would be in Paradise did not utter the word of testimony in his testimony for them; rather he said: "Abu Bakr is in Paradise, 'Umar is in Paradise, 'Uthman is in Paradise, 'Ali is in Paradise," and so on in the hadith.

The Muslims have agreed that if a disbeliever says, "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," he has entered Islam and has testified to the truth, and his Islam does not depend on the word of testimony. And [it is established] that he has entered the Prophet's saying: "until they testify that there is no god but Allah." In another wording: "until they say there is no god but Allah." This indicates that their mere saying "There is no god but Allah" is a testimony from them. This is more than can be cited in its evidences from the Book and the Sunnah. So there is no evidence on which those who require the word of testimony can rely. And Allah knows best.

Section.

**Section on the Stage of Informing and Reporting**

As for the stage of informing and reporting (al-i'lam wal-ikhbar), it has two kinds: informing by speech (i'lam bil-qawl) and informing by action (i'lam bil-fi'l). This is the case with everyone who informs another of a matter. Sometimes he informs him by his words and sometimes by his deeds. For this reason, whoever turns a house into a mosque, opens its door to everyone who enters, and calls the adhan for prayer in it, has informed others that it is a waqf (endowment), even though he has not uttered it. Likewise, whoever is seen drawing near to another through various kinds of gifts (al-masar) makes known to him and to others that he loves him, even though he does not say it with his tongue. The same applies in reverse.

Similarly, the testimony of the Lord, exalted is His majesty, and His clarification and informing, occur sometimes by His speech and sometimes by His action. The speech is what He sent through His messengers and what He revealed in His books. It is known necessarily (bil-idtirar) that all the messengers reported from Allah that He bore witness to Himself that there is no god but Him, and He informed of this, and He commanded His servants to bear witness to it. His testimony, glory be to Him, that there is no god but Him, is known through every person who conveyed His words.

As for His clarifying and informing by His action, it is what His report, exalted is He, contains about the signs that indicate His oneness, whose indication is known by reason and innate nature (al-fitrah). The term "testimony" (shahadah) is also used for this, just as the term "indication" (dalalah), "guidance" (irshad) and "clarification" (bayan) are used. The indicator (dalil) makes clear and manifests what it indicates, just as the witness and the informant make it clear. Indeed, clarification by action may be more manifest and more eloquent. The evidence of circumstances (shahid al-hal) may also be called speech, utterance and words, because it stands in for speech and performs its function, as it has been said:

"The two eyes said to him: hearing and obedience, and they shed pearls before they were pierced."

Another said:

"My camel complained to me of the length of the journey: patient endurance, for we are both tested."

Another said:

"The basin became full and the pool said: Enough, gently, you have filled my belly."

This is also called testimony, as in His saying: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while bearing witness against themselves of disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 17]. This is their testimony against themselves through what they do of deeds and statements of disbelief, so it is a testimony to their disbelief, and they are witnesses against themselves by what it testifies to.

The purpose is that Allah, glory be to Him, bears witness through what He made His created signs to be indicators of Him, for their indication is only by His creation and His making. He also bears witness through His verbal, spoken signs, which agree with what His created signs testify to. Thus the testimony of speech and the testimony of action agree, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We will show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53], meaning that the Qur'an is true. He informed that He indicates, through His signs on the horizons and within the self, the truthfulness of His verbal, spoken signs. This act-testimony has been mentioned by more than one of the imams of Arabic grammar and tafsir. Ibn Kaysan said: Allah bore witness, through His wondrous governance and His firm affairs in His creation, that there is no god but Him.

**Section**

As for the fourth stage, which is the command to that and the obligation of it, although mere testimony does not necessarily entail it, nevertheless testimony in this context indicates it and includes it. He, glory be to Him, bore witness to it as one who judges, decides, commands and obligates His servants to it, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him﴾ [al-Isra': 23]. He said: ﴿Allah said: Do not take two gods; He is only one God﴾ [al-Nahl: 51]. He said: ﴿They were commanded only to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5]. He said: ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god﴾ [al-Isra': 22]. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ [al-Qasas: 88]. The entire Qur'an bears witness to this.

The way in which His testimony, glory be to Him, entails this is that when He testifies that there is no god but Him, He has informed, clarified, made known, judged and decided that whatever else is other than Him is not a god, that the divinity of anything other than Him is the falsest of falsehoods, and that affirming it is the greatest injustice. Therefore none deserves worship besides Him, just as divinity is not suitable for anyone else. That entails the command to take Him alone as god and the prohibition of taking anything else along with Him as a god. The addressee understands this from this affirmation and negation, just as when you see a man asking for a legal opinion (yastaftī), or seeking testimony, or seeking medical treatment from one who is not qualified for that, and leaving the one who is qualified, you say: This is not a mufti, nor a witness, nor a physician; the mufti is so-and-so, the witness is so-and-so, and the physician is so-and-so. This is indeed a command and a prohibition from you.

Moreover, the proofs have indicated that He, glory be to Him, alone deserves worship. So when He informs that He alone is the one who deserves worship, this report includes commanding and obligating the servants to perform what the Lord, exalted is He, deserves from them, and that fulfilling this is the pure right owed to Him by them. Thus when He, glory be to Him, testifies that there is no god but Him, His testimony includes the command and obligation to His monotheism (tawhid).

Moreover, the words "judgment" (hukm) and "decision" (qada') are used for declarative sentences. A declarative sentence is called a proposition (qadiyyah) and a judgment, and one is said to have judged in it such-and-such. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed they say, out of their lie: Allah has begotten. And indeed they are liars. Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Saffat: 151-154]. Here He made their bare report a judgment. In another place He said: ﴿Shall We make the Muslims like the criminals? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 35]. But this is a judgment without obligation. The judgment and decision that there is no god but Him, however, includes obligation. And Allah, glory be to Him, knows best.

**[Section: Explanation of His saying "standing in justice"]**

**Section**

As for His saying: ﴿standing in justice﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]:

"Al-qist" (justice) means 'adl (justice, equity). Allah, glory be to Him, bore witness that He stands in justice in His monotheism, and in His oneness in His justice. Tawhid and 'adl are the sum of the attributes of perfection, for tawhid includes His being singular, glory be to Him, in perfection, majesty, glory and exaltation, which is not fitting for anyone other than Him. And 'adl includes that all His acts occur in rightness, correctness and conformity with wisdom.

This is the tawhid and justice of the messengers: affirming the attributes, commanding the worship of Allah alone with no partner for Him, and affirming the decree (qadar), the wisdoms, and the praiseworthy objectives and ends by His act and His command. It is not the tawhid of the Jahmiyyah (a sect that denied divine attributes), the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist sect), and the Qadariyyah (a sect that denied divine decree), which is the denial of the attributes and the realities of the Most Beautiful Names. Nor is their justice, which is denying the decree, or negating the wisdoms, ends and praiseworthy consequences for which Allah acts and commands. His standing in justice, glory be to Him, in His testimony includes several matters.

The first: that He stands in justice in this testimony, which is the most just testimony absolutely, and denying or rejecting it is the greatest injustice absolutely. There is no more just than tawhid and no more unjust than shirk. He, glory be to Him, stands in justice in this testimony in speech and in action, in that He bore witness to it, informed and made known to His servants, clarified for them its realization and its soundness, obligated them to its requirements, judged by it, made reward and punishment dependent upon it, and made commands and prohibitions among its rights and duties. So the entire religion is among its rights, all reward is upon it, and all punishment is upon abandoning it.

This is the justice with which the Lord, exalted is He, stands in this testimony. His commands are all a perfecting of it and a command to fulfil its rights. His prohibitions are all a safeguard for it against what diminishes and opposes it. His reward is all upon it, and His punishment is all upon abandoning it and abandoning its rights. His creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them was by it and for its sake. It is the truth (al-haqq) by which they were created. Its opposite is falsehood and aimlessness, from which He declared Himself free, and He informed that He did not create the heavens and the earth with it. He, exalted is He, said, refuting the polytheists who deny this testimony: ﴿We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad: 27].

He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. But those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 1-3].

He said: ﴿It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the account. Allah did not create that except in truth﴾ [Yunus: 5].

He said: ﴿Do they not reflect within themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. But indeed many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers﴾ [al-Rum: 8]. He said: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except in truth﴾ [al-Dukhan: 38-39]. This is abundant in the Qur'an. The truth by which the heavens and the earth were created and for which they exist is tawhid, along with its rights of command and prohibition, reward and punishment. So the legislation (shar') and the decree (qadar), the creation and the command, the reward and the punishment, all stand in justice, and tawhid issues from them both. This is the straight path upon which the Lord, glory be to Him and exalted is He, stands.

He, exalted is He, said, recounting of His prophet Hud: ﴿Indeed I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56]. He, glory be to Him, is upon a straight path in His speech and His action. He speaks the truth and does justice: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; none can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing. And Allah speaks the truth and He guides to the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 115, 4].

So the straight path upon which our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, is the requirement of tawhid and justice. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah presents an example: two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything, a burden upon his master, wherever he directs him he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path?﴾ [al-Nahl: 76]. This is an example Allah struck for Himself and for the idol. He is the One who commands justice and is on a straight path, while the idol is the likeness of the servant who is a burden upon his master: wherever he directs him, he brings no good.

The purpose here: His saying, ﴿standing in justice﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18], is like His saying, ﴿Indeed my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56]. His saying ﴿qā'iman bil-qist﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18] is in the accusative as a *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier, a clause describing the state of the subject at the time of the action). There are two possibilities. The first is that it is a *ḥāl* of the doer in "shahida Allāh" (God bore witness), and the governing element is the verb. The meaning on this reading is: God bore witness, in the state of standing in justice, that there is no god but Him. The second is that it is a *ḥāl* of the pronoun in "huwa" (He), and the governing element is the sense of negation, that is, "there is no god but He," in the state of His being one who stands in justice. There is a clear difference between the two readings. The first reading implies that the meaning is: God bore witness, speaking justice, informing of it, commanding it, doing it, and recompensing by it, that there is no god but He. Justice applies to speech and to action, and the one who is *muqsit* (just) is the one who is just in his speech and his deed. So God bore witness, standing in justice in speech and in deed, that there is no god but He. This establishes that this testimony is a testimony of justice and equity, and it is the most just testimony, just as the thing testified to is the most just, the most correct and the most deserving of all things. Ibn al-Sa'ib and others mentioned, regarding the occasion of revelation of the verse, what bears witness to this. It is that "two rabbis from the rabbis of Syria came to the Prophet ﷺ. When they saw Medina, one of them said to his companion: 'How much this city resembles the city of the Prophet who will emerge at the end of time.' When they entered upon the Prophet ﷺ they said to him: 'Are you Muhammad?' He said: 'Yes.' 'And Ahmad?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'We ask you about a testimony. If you inform us of it, we will believe in you.' He said: 'Ask me.' They said: 'Inform us about the greatest testimony in the Book of God.' Then the verse was revealed: ﴿God bears witness that there is no god but He﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18], to the end of the verse." Since standing in justice occurs in speech and in deed, the meaning is that He, glorified is He, bears witness while standing in justice and knowing it, not in injustice. This testimony includes speech and action, for it includes that He is the one who alone deserves worship, to the exclusion of others; that those who worship Him alone are the successful, the happy; and that those who associate others with Him are the misguided, the wretched. So when He bears witness, standing in justice, which includes the recompense of the sincere with Paradise and the recompense of the polytheists with the Fire, this is part of the complete requirement of the testimony and its realization. His saying ﴿qā'iman bil-qist﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18] is thus an indication of the recompense of the one who bears witness to it and of the one who denies it. And God knows best.

(Section)

As for the second possibility, namely that His saying "qā'iman" is a *ḥāl* of what comes after *illā* (except), the meaning is: there is no god but He, standing in justice. He alone deserves divinity, together with His being one who stands in justice. My shaykh said: "This reading is preferable, for it implies that the angels and those possessed of knowledge bear witness to Him that there is no god but He, and that He stands in justice."

I say: His intention is that when His saying ﴿qā'iman bil-qist﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18] is a *ḥāl* of the one testified to, it is like an attribute of Him, for the *ḥāl* is, in meaning, a description of its owner. When the testimony falls upon the one in the state and its owner, both become the thing testified to. Thus the angels and those possessed of knowledge have testified that He stands in justice, just as they testified that there is no god but He. The first reading does not imply this, for if the reading is "God bore witness, standing in justice, that there is no god but He, and the angels and those possessed of knowledge bear witness that there is no god but He," then standing in justice is a *ḥāl* of the name of God alone.

Furthermore, His being one who stands in justice in what He testified to is more emphatic than His being a *ḥāl* of the bare testimony.

If it is said: If it is a *ḥāl* of "huwa" (He), why was it not placed adjacent to it? And why was it separated between the owner of the *ḥāl* and the *ḥāl* by the conjoined element, so that it comes in the middle between the owner of the *ḥāl* and itself?

I say: Its benefit is evident. If He had said: "God bore witness that there is no god but He, standing in justice, and the angels and those possessed of knowledge," it would have given the false impression that "the angels and those possessed of knowledge" are conjoined to the pronoun in His saying ﴿qā'iman bil-qist﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]. But the conjunction is not suitable because of the separation, and the meaning is definitely not that. The meaning is the opposite of that, namely that His standing in justice is specific to Him, just as divinity is specific to Him. He alone is the God who is worshipped and deserves worship, and He alone is the one who recompenses, rewards and punishes with justice.

His saying: "There is no god but He." Muhammad ibn Ja'far mentioned that he said: "The first is a description and a declaration of oneness (tawhid), and the second is a formula and instruction, that is, say: 'There is no god but He.'" The meaning of this is: the first includes that God, glorified is He, bore witness to it and informed of it, and the one who recites the Qur'an only informs of His testimony; there is no testimony in that from the reciter himself. So He, glorified is He, repeated its mention alone so that the reciter may say it, and thus he too would be a witness.

Furthermore, the first is information about the testimony to oneness, and the second is information about oneness itself. He concluded with His saying: ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]. So the verse includes His oneness, His justice, His might and His wisdom. Oneness includes the affirmation of the attributes of His perfection and the qualities of His majesty, the absence of any like Him in these, and His worship alone without any partner. Justice includes His placing things in their proper place and assigning them to their proper stations, and that He did not single out anything of them except by a specifier that required it, and that He does not punish one who does not deserve punishment, nor withhold from one who deserves reward, even if it is He who made him deserving. Might includes the completeness of His power, strength and dominance. Wisdom includes the completeness of His knowledge and expertise, and that He commands and forbids, creates and decrees, for wisdoms and beneficial ends in which He deserves complete praise.

So His name "the Mighty" includes sovereignty, and His name "the Wise" includes praise. The beginning of the verse includes oneness, and that is the reality of "there is no god but God alone, without partner, to Him belongs sovereignty and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things capable." This is the best thing said by the Messenger of God ﷺ and the prophets before him. The Wise is the one who, when He commands something, it is good in itself; when He forbids something, it is ugly in itself; when He informs of something, it is true; when He does an act, it is right; and when He wills something, it is more deserving of being willed than anything else. This attribute in its perfection belongs to God alone.

This verse and this testimony therefore include the indication of His unity, which negates polytheism; of His justice, which negates injustice; of His might, which negates incapacity; and of His wisdom, which negates ignorance and defect. So in it is the testimony to Him of oneness, justice, power, knowledge and wisdom. For this reason it is the greatest testimony.

None of the sects can uphold this testimony in its correct form except the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna). The other sects of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'a) do not uphold it. The philosophers are the most intense in denying and rejecting its content from its beginning to its end. The groups of the monist unitarians (al-Ittihadiyya) are the farthest of God's creation from it in every respect. The Jahmiyya deny its reality in several respects:

Among them: the deity (ilah) is the one whom hearts worship (ta'allah) out of love for Him, longing for Him and turning to Him in repentance. Yet in their view God does not love and is not loved.

Among them: the testimony is His speech and His information about what He testified to, while in their view He does not speak, nor speak, nor bear witness, nor inform.

Among them: it includes His distinction from His creation in His essence and attributes. Yet according to their Pharaonic faction, He is not distinct from creation and does not dwell with it; there is no god above the Throne to be worshipped, nor a lord to whom one prays and prostrates.

According to their incarnationist faction (hulūliyya), He is present in every place in His essence, even in the places one is ashamed to mention. These are the affirming Jahmiyya, and those are their negators.

Among them: His standing in justice in His acts and His speech. In their view, no act or speech has ever subsisted in Him or ever subsists in Him, and His speech is created, one of the created things, and His act is the separate effect. As for His having an act by which He is truly an agent, no.

Among them: justice, in their view, has no reality. Rather every possible thing is justice, and there is nothing within His capability that would be injustice or justice. Injustice in their view is the impossible which is impossible in its essence, and justice is the possible. So God, glorified is He, according to their claim, has exonerated Himself from the impossible which is impossible in its essence and which does not fall under power.

Among them: might is power and capacity. In their view no attribute subsists in Him, and He has no attribute called power or strength.

Among them: wisdom is the end for the sake of which He acts, which is the desired object of the act, and whose existence is preferable to its non-existence. In their view this is impossible with regard to Him, glorified is He. So He does not act for a wisdom or an end. Rather there is no end to His act or command, and there is nothing but bare will stripped of wisdom and causation.

Among them: the deity is the one who has the most beautiful names and the highest attributes, who acts by His power, will and wisdom, who is described by attributes and acts, who is named by names whose realities and meanings subsist in Him. Only the followers of the Messengers affirm this in its true sense, and they are the people of justice and oneness.

(Section: The claims of the Jahmiyya and the Mu'tazila)

The Jahmiyya and the Mu'tazila claim that His essence is not loved, that His face is not seen, that one does not take delight in looking at it, and that hearts do not long for Him. In reality they are deniers of divinity.

The Qadariyya deny that the acts of the angels, jinn, humans and all animals fall under His power, will and creation. In reality, they deny His complete might and dominion.

The Jabriyya deny His wisdom and that in His acts and commands there is an end for which He acts and commands. In reality, they deny His wisdom and praiseworthiness.

The followers of Ibn Sina, al-Nasir al-Tusi and their offspring deny that there is any quiddity (mahiyya) other than absolute existence, and that He has any affirmative attribute additional to the quiddity of existence. In reality, they deny His essence, attributes and acts, and they are not shy about this.

The monist unitarians (al-Ittihadiyya) are more calamitous and more bitter, for they have demolished the foundations from the root. They said: there is no existence of a Creator and existence of a created thing; rather the created, which is likened, is the very essence of the Truth which is exalted; all of that is from a single essence, indeed it is the single essence.

This great testimony: all of these people are not standing by it, and it includes the refutation of what they hold and its rejection, just as it included the refutation of what the polytheists hold and its rejection. It nullifies the position of both the sects of polytheism and of nullification (ta'til). Only the people of affirmation (ahl al-ithbat) stand by this testimony, those who affirm for God what He affirmed for Himself of names and attributes, who negate from Him the likeness of created things, and who worship Him alone, not associating anything with Him.

(Section: His testimony, glorified is He, includes His clarification to the servants, guiding them and making them know what He testified to)

Since His testimony, glorified is He, includes His clarifying to the servants, guiding them and making them know what He testified to, otherwise, if He had testified a testimony they could not know, they would not benefit from it, and the proof would not be established against them by it. Just as when a human witness has a testimony but does not clarify it, rather conceals it, no one benefits from it and no proof is established by it. And since no one benefits from it except by its clarification, He, glorified is He, has clarified it to the utmost clarity by three means: hearing, sight and reason.

As for hearing: by hearing His recited verbal signs, which include the affirmation of the attributes of His perfection and the qualities of His majesty, His elevation above His Throne above His seven heavens, His speaking through His books, and His addressing whom He wills of His servants, speaking and addressing in reality, not metaphorically.

This refutes the view of those who say that He did not intend for His servants what His revelatory verses indicate, namely affirming their meanings and realities for which their words were coined. This view is the opposite of clarification and declaration, and it returns to the purpose of testimony with nullification and concealment. God has condemned whoever conceals a testimony he holds from God, and He has informed us that such a person is among the greatest wrongdoers. If a servant possesses a testimony from God that confirms what His Messenger brought of the signs of prophethood, the Oneness taught by all the messengers, and that Abraham and all his family were upon Islam, and then he conceals this testimony, he is among the greatest wrongdoers, as the enemies of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) among the Jews did, for they knew him as they know their own sons. How then could it be supposed of God, glorified is He, that He concealed the testimony of truth, which the Jahmiyya, the Mu'tazila and the Mu'attila bear witness to, while He does not bear witness to it for Himself, and instead bears witness for Himself to what opposes and contradicts it, and is in no way compatible with it? Glory be to You, this is a tremendous slander!

God, glorified is He, bore witness for Himself that He is established upon the Throne, that He is the Subduer above His servants, that His angels fear Him from above them, that the angels ascend to Him with the command and descend from Him with it, that good deeds ascend to Him, that He comes and approaches, that He speaks, is pleased and angered, loves and hates, is harmed, rejoices and laughs, that He hears and sees, and that the believers will see Him with their eyes on the day they meet Him, along with other things He witnessed for Himself and His messengers witnessed for Him. The Jahmiyya bore witness to the opposite of all this, and said: "Our testimony is more correct and more just than the testimony of the texts, for the texts contain the concealment of truth and the display of its opposite."

The Lord's testimony refutes these people in the strongest terms, and it implies that what He testified to He has made clear, explained and manifested, to the point that He placed it at the highest levels of manifestation and clarity. Furthermore, if the truth were what the Mu'attila and the Jahmiyya say, then the servants would not have benefited from what God, glorified is He, testified to, for the truth in reality, according to them, is not what He testified to for Himself. What He testified to for Himself and made manifest and clear is not true, and it is not permissible to derive from it truth and certainty.

As for His visible, created signs, reflecting on them and deducing from them, they indicate what His verbal, revelatory signs indicate. The signs of the Lord are His proofs and demonstrations by which the servants know Him, and by which they know His names, attributes, Oneness, command and prohibition. The messengers inform about Him through His speech which He spoke, which are His verbal signs, and they derive proof for this from His acts, which attest to the truth of this, and which are His visible signs. Reason combines these and that, and so it affirms with certainty the truth of what the messengers brought. Thus the testimony of revelation, sight, reason and natural disposition agree. Glorified is He, for the perfection of His justice, mercy, beneficence, wisdom, His love of excuses and His establishment of proof, did not send any prophet except with him a sign indicating his truthfulness in what he reported. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that people may establish justice﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the reminder if you do not know, with clear proofs and scriptures﴾ [al-Nahl: 43]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There have certainly come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you have said. So why did you kill them, if you are truthful? And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied, who came with clear proofs and scriptures and the illuminating Book﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 183-184]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied﴾ [Fatir: 4]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they deny you, those before them denied, when their messengers came to them with clear proofs and with scriptures and the illuminating Book﴾ [Fatir: 25].

Indeed, among the most hidden of the signs of the messengers are the signs of Hud (peace be upon him), to the point that his people said to him: ﴿O Hud, you have brought us no clear proof﴾ [Hud: 53]. Yet his proof is among the most manifest of proofs, and he alluded to it when he said: ﴿Indeed I call God to witness, and you bear witness that I am free from what you associate besides Him. So scheme against me all together, then do not give me respite. Indeed I have relied upon God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 54-56]. This is among the greatest signs: that a single man addresses a great nation with this address, not fearful, not anxious, not weak, but confident in what he said and certain of it. He called God first to witness his freedom from their religion and from what they are upon, calling as one confident in Him, relying upon Him, informing his people that He is his protector and helper, and that He would not give them power over him.

Then he called them to witness, as one openly declaring opposition to them, that he is free from their religion and their gods, to which they pledge allegiance and enmity, and for whose support they spend their blood and wealth.

Then he reinforced this by treating them with contempt, belittling them and disdaining them, and that even if they all gathered together against him, to satisfy their rage against him, and then sought to deal with him without giving him respite, then within this is the implication that they are weaker, more incapable and lesser than that, and that if you were to attempt it, you would return in your rage humiliated and forsaken.

Then he established his call in the finest manner, and made clear that his Lord and their Lord, whose hands hold their forelocks, is his protector and his trustee, who undertakes his support and his strengthening, and that He is upon a straight path. So He does not forsake whoever relies upon Him and believes in Him, nor does He give His enemies cause to gloat over him, nor does He stand with them against him, for His straight path, which He is upon in His saying and His doing, prevents this and refuses it.

Under this address is the fact that among His straight path is that He takes vengeance upon whoever departs from it and acts contrary to it, and brings down His might upon him, for the straight path is the justice upon which the Lord, exalted is He, stands. From it is His vengeance upon the people of polytheism and sin, His support of His friends and messengers against their enemies, and that He takes them away and replaces them with other people, without that harming Him at all. And He, glorified is He, is the one who stands over everything, guarding, caring for, managing and counting it.

What sign, proof and evidence is better than the signs, proofs and arguments of the prophets? These are a testimony from God, glorified is He, to them, which He made clear to His servants to the utmost degree of clarity, and which He manifested to them to the utmost degree of manifestation, through His speech and His deed. In the authentic collection, from him (ﷺ), he said: "There is no prophet among the prophets but that he was given signs such that people believed upon their like, and what I was given was a revelation which God revealed to me, so I hope to be the one with the most followers on the Day of Resurrection."

Among His names, exalted is He, is al-Mu'min (the Giver of Security/the Affirmer), which in one of the two interpretations means the one who confirms the truthful by establishing for them the evidences of their truthfulness. He is the one who confirmed His messengers and prophets in what they conveyed from Him, and bore witness that they are truthful through the proofs by which He demonstrated their truthfulness, both in decree and creation. God, glorified is He, informed, and His report is truth and His word is the reality, that He will surely show His servants, from the horizons and from themselves, signs which make clear to them that the revelation His messengers conveyed is true. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53], meaning the Qur'an, for it is what was mentioned before in His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if it is from God and you disbelieve in it?﴾ [Fussilat: 52]. Then He said: ﴿Is it not sufficient that your Lord is witness over all things?﴾ [Fussilat: 53]. Thus, glorified is He, bore witness to His Messenger by His saying that what he brought is true, and promised him that He would show the servants from His active, created signs what also bears witness to this. Then He mentioned something greater and more magnificent than that, which is His witnessing, glorified is He, over all things. Among His names is al-Shahid (the Witness), who nothing hides from, and from whom not even the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven escapes. Rather, He is aware of everything, present with everything, and knowing its details. This is a proof by His names and attributes. The first is a proof by His speech and words, and proof by the horizons and the selves is a proof by His acts and creatures.

If you say: I have understood proof by His words and proof by His creatures, so explain to me how to prove by His names and attributes, for this is something we have no familiarity with in our discourse and books.

I say: Indeed! By God's life, it is as you have mentioned, and His affair is greater and higher. For the Lord, exalted is He, is the one indicated, and His signs are the indicator and the proof.

Know that God, glorified is He, in reality is the one who indicates Himself through His signs. He is the proof for His servants in reality, through the indications and signs He set up for them. He has deposited in natural dispositions that have not been tainted by negation and denial that He, glorified is He, is perfect in His names and attributes, and that He is described by every perfection, transcendent above every defect and deficiency. So all perfection, beauty, majesty, splendor, might, greatness and magnificence are inseparable from His essence. It is impossible for Him to be otherwise. So all life belongs to Him, all knowledge belongs to Him, all power belongs to Him, and hearing, sight, will, volition, mercy, self-sufficiency, generosity, beneficence and kindness all belong exclusively to Him and subsist in Him. What of His perfection is hidden from the creation is far greater, and far greater than what they know of it. Rather, there is no comparison between what they know of it and what they do not know.

Among His sacred perfection is His awareness of everything and His witnessing over it, such that no aspect of its details escapes Him, nor any atom of its particles, outwardly or inwardly. And one who is of this description: how is it fitting for the servants to associate others with Him, to worship others along with Him, or to make another god with Him? And how is it fitting for His perfection that He would let stand one who lies against Him in the greatest lie, and informs about Him contrary to what is the case, then supports him in that, strengthens him, exalts his word, raises his status, answers his call, destroys his enemy, and manifests at his hands signs, proofs and evidences which the strength of humans cannot match, and yet he is, despite all that, a liar against Him, a fabricator, striving in the earth for corruption?

It is known that His witnessing over everything, His power over everything, His wisdom, His might and His sacred perfection reject that in every way. Whoever thinks this of Him and permits it upon Him is among the furthest of creatures from knowing Him, even if some of His attributes are known to him, such as the attribute of power and the attribute of will.

The Qur'an is full of this method, which is the method of the elite. Indeed, the elite of the elite are those who derive proof of God from His acts, and from what it is fitting for Him to do and what it is fitting for Him not to do.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 3, verse 18 (part 7 of 8):

When you reflect upon the Qur'an, you will see it calling out to this, presenting it and repeating it to the one who has understanding and a heart attentive to Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have severed from him the aorta, and not one of you could have held Us off from him.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44] Do you not see how He, glorified is He, informs that His perfection, His wisdom and His power refuse to let stand one who fabricates sayings against Him? Rather, He must make him an example for His servants, as His custom has run concerning those who fabricate against Him. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"? So if Allah willed, He would seal over your heart﴾ [al-Shura: 24]. Here the answer of the condition ends, then He gave a definite report, not conditional: that He ﴿erases falsehood and establishes the truth﴾ [al-Shura: 24]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said, "Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being."﴾ [al-An'am: 91]. So He informed that whoever denies that He sends messengers and speaks has not measured Him with His true measure, nor known Him as He should be known, nor magnified Him as He deserves. How then could one who thinks that He supports the liar who fabricates against Him, and strengthens him, and manifests upon his hands the signs and proofs? This is very frequent in the Qur'an: His holy perfection, His attributes and His majesty are used as evidence for the truthfulness of His messengers, for His promise and His threat, and He calls His servants to that. Just as His names and attributes are used as evidence for His oneness and for the falsehood of association (shirk), as in His saying: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ [al-Hashr: 22-23], and multiples upon multiples of that in the Qur'an.

And He, glorified is He, uses His names and attributes as evidence for the falsehood of the rulings and false laws attributed to Him, and that His holy perfection prevents their being legislated. As in His saying: ﴿And when they commit an indecency they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us with it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 28], and His saying, after mentioning what He forbade and prohibited of shirk, injustice, indecencies and speaking about Him without knowledge: ﴿All of that - its evil is hateful in the sight of your Lord﴾ [al-Isra': 38]. So He informed you that whatever is evil in itself, He hates it, and His perfection refuses that He make it a law and religion for Himself. He, glorified is He, guides His servants by His names and attributes to what He does and commands, what He loves and hates, what He rewards for and punishes for. But this path is not reached except by the elite of the elite. Therefore the method of the common people was indications by visible signs, for it is broader and easier to take up. Allah, glorified is He, favours some of His creation over others, and raises the ranks of whom He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

The Great Qur'an has gathered together what has not been gathered in anything else. It is the call and the proof, it is the evidence and that which is evidenced, it is the witness and that to which witness is borne, it is the judgment and the proof, it is the claim and the clear evidence. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it?﴾ [Hud: 17], meaning from his Lord, which is the Qur'an. And Allah the Exalted said to one who asked for a sign indicating the truthfulness of His Messenger: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe. Say, "Sufficient is Allah as witness between me and you; He knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believed in falsehood and disbelieved in Allah - those are the losers."﴾ [al-Ankabut: 51-52]. So He, glorified is He, informed that the Book He sent down upon His Messenger suffices in place of every sign, for in it is the proof and the indication that it is from Allah, and that Allah, glorified is He, sent His Messenger with it, and in it is the explanation of what necessitates happiness for whoever follows it and saves him from punishment. Then He said: ﴿Say, "Sufficient is Allah as witness between me and you; He knows what is in the heavens and the earth"﴾ [al-Ankabut: 52]. So when Allah, glorified is He, knows all things, His testimony is the most truthful and most just testimony, for it is testimony with complete knowledge that encompasses the thing witnessed. Thus the one who bears witness is the most just and truthful of witnesses. He, glorified is He, mentions His knowledge when He bears witness, His power and dominion when He recompenses, His wisdom when He creates and commands, His mercy when mentioning the sending of His Messenger, His forbearance when mentioning the sins and disobediences of His servants, His hearing when mentioning their supplication, and His being asked, His might and His knowledge when decreeing and determining.

So reflect on the occurrence of His Most Beautiful Names in His Book, and their connection to creation and command, reward and punishment.

[Section: Citing Allah's testimony for the Messenger's prophethood]

Section

And from this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as witness between me and you, and those who have knowledge of the Book."﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43]

So He cited, for His messenger's prophethood, the testimony of Allah to him, and it is necessary that this testimony be known, and that the proof be established by it against those who deny him. Likewise His saying: ﴿Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you."﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. Likewise His saying: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you - He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And sufficient is Allah as witness.﴾ [al-Nisa': 166]. Likewise His saying: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an, indeed you are among the messengers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 1-3], and His saying: ﴿These are the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 252], and His saying: ﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His messenger﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1], and His saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

All of this is testimony from Him to His Messenger, which He has manifested and clarified, and clarified its correctness to the utmost clarity, such that He cut off the excuse between Him and His servants and established the proof against them. That He, glorified is He, is a witness to His Messenger is known by all kinds of evidence: rational, transmitted, innate, necessary and reflective.

Whoever considers this and reflects upon it will know that Allah, glorified is He, bore witness to His Messenger with the most truthful, most just and most manifest testimony, and confirmed him in every kind of confirmation: by His speech, which established proofs of its truthfulness; by His deeds and His approval; and by what He instilled in His servants of acknowledging His perfection and His being free of blemishes and whatever is unfitting for Him. At every time He brings forth signs that indicate the truthfulness of His Messenger, by which He establishes the proof and removes the excuse, and by which He judges for him and his followers with what He promised them of honour, salvation, victory and support, and judges against his enemies and deniers with what He threatened them: of disgrace, punishment and immediate penalties, which indicate the realization of the deferred penalties. ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, and sufficient is Allah as witness﴾ [al-Fath: 28]. So He makes it prevail in two ways: a prevailing by proof, explanation and indication, and a prevailing by help, victory, dominance and support, until He makes it prevail over its opponents and he is victorious.

And His saying: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you - He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness﴾ [al-Nisa': 166]. What is in it of the report of Allah's knowledge, which no other can act upon, is among the greatest testimony that it is He who sent it down, as He said in the other verse: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful." And if they do not respond to you, then know that it has been sent down with the knowledge of Allah, and that there is no deity except Him. Will you then be Muslims?﴾ [Hud: 13-14].

The meaning is not merely the report that He sent it down, which is known to Him as He knows all things, for everything is known to Him, true and false. Rather the meaning is: He sent it down containing His knowledge. So its descent containing His knowledge is the sign that it is from Him, and that it is truth and sincerity. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Say, "It has sent it down, He who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth"﴾ [al-Furqan: 6], which He mentioned, glorified is He, as denial and refutation of the one who said, "He has fabricated it."

[Section: Among His testimony is what He placed in the hearts of His servants of firm affirmation of His speech and revelation]

Section

And among His testimony also is what He placed in the hearts of His servants: firm affirmation, established certainty, and tranquillity in His speech and revelation. For custom makes it impossible that such a thing be attained by what is among the greatest lies and fabrication against the Lord of the worlds, and reporting about Him contrary to what He is in His names and attributes. Rather that produces the greatest doubt and suspicion, and sound natures and minds reject it, just as the natures with which animals were created reject harmful, filthy foods that do not nourish, such as urine and foulness. For Allah, glorified is He, created hearts to accept the truth and submit to it, to be at peace with it, to rest in it and to love it; and He created them to hate falsehood and lies, to shun them, to doubt them, and not to rest in them. And if natures were left in their state, they would not prefer anything over the truth, would not be at rest except in it, would not be tranquil except by it, and would not love anything other than it. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, urged His servants to reflect upon the Qur'an, for everyone who reflects upon it, his reflection makes necessary for him a necessary knowledge and a firm certainty that it is truth and sincerity, indeed the most true of all truth and most sincere of all sincerity, and that the one who brought it is the most truthful of Allah's creation, the most righteous, and the most complete in knowledge, action and recognition. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction.﴾ [al-Nisa': 82]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24]. So if the locks were removed from the hearts, the realities of the Qur'an would touch them, the lamps of faith would shine within them, and you would know with a necessary knowledge, which would be with them like other matters of direct experience - joy, pain, love and fear - that it is from Allah, that He spoke it truly, and that His messenger Jibril conveyed it from Him to His Messenger Muhammad. This inner witness in the heart is among the greatest of witnesses. With it Heraclius argued against Abu Sufyan when he said to him: "Does anyone of them turn back in disgust at his religion after entering it?" He said: "No." He said: "Thus is faith when its sweetness mixes with the cheerfulness of hearts; no one is disgusted with it." Allah the Exalted has pointed to this meaning in His saying: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾ [al-Ankabut: 49], and His saying: ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so they believe in it﴾ [al-Hajj: 54], and His saying: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth﴾ [Saba': 6], and His saying: ﴿Is one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19], and His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why has not a sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance"﴾ [al-Ra'd: 27]. Meaning: the sign they propose does not bring guidance; rather Allah is the One who guides and sends astray. Then He drew their attention to the greatest and most majestic sign, which is the tranquillity of the hearts of the believers through His remembrance which He sent down, saying: ﴿Those who believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28], that is, by His Book and His speech: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah are hearts assured﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28]. So the tranquillity of sound hearts and upright natures in it, and their rest in it, is among the greatest signs; for it is impossible by custom that hearts be at peace and rest in lies, fabrication and falsehood.

If it is said: Why did Allah, glorified is He, not mention the testimony of His messengers along with the angels, saying: "Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and the messengers," and they are greater in testimony than those of knowledge?

It is said: In this there are several benefits.

The first of them: those of knowledge are more general than the messengers and prophets, so they include them and their followers.

Second: the mention of "those possessed of knowledge" (ulu al-ʿilm) in this testimony, and its being attached to them, indicates that it is one of the requirements and necessary consequences of knowledge. Whoever is among those possessed of knowledge bears this testimony, just as one says: when the crescent moon rises and becomes clear, everyone who has the faculty of sight sees it. And when a clear fragrance spreads, everyone who has a sense of smell perceives it. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And Hellfire is made manifest to whoever can see﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 36], meaning everyone who has sight will see it then, plainly. In this there is an explanation that whoever is not witnessed to by God, glorified is He, in this testimony, is among the greatest of the ignorant, even if he knows of worldly affairs what no one else knows. He is among those of ignorance, not among those possessed of knowledge. We have already shown that no one upholds this testimony and renders it correctly except the followers of the Messengers, the people of affirmation (ahl al-ithbat). They are those possessed of knowledge, and all others are of ignorance, even if they expand their speech and multiply their disputation.

Third: God's testimony to the people of this testimony, that they are those possessed of knowledge. His testimony for them is more just and more truthful than the testimony of the Jahmiyya (followers of Jahm ibn Safwan, a sect that denied God's attributes), the Mu'attila (those who negate divine attributes), and the Pharaonists (those who liken the denial of God's attributes to Pharaoh's denial) that they are ignorant, that they are Hashwiyya (a derogatory term for literalists), that they are Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists), that they are Mujassima (those who ascribe a body to God), and Nawabit and Nawasib (derogatory terms for those who hate ʿAli or the Prophet's household). The most truthful of the truthful suffices them, testifying that they are among those possessed of knowledge, since they bore witness to Him with the reality of what He bore witness to for Himself, without distortion or negation, and affirmed for Him the true reality and content of this testimony. Their opponents negated its realities from Him and affirmed for Him only its words and figurative meanings.

[Section: Within the divine testimony is praise of those possessed of knowledge who bear witness to it, and their justification]

Within this divine testimony is praise of the people of knowledge who bear witness to it, and their vindication. For He, glorified is He, joined their testimony with His own testimony and that of His angels, and called them as witnesses – the Exalted – to a great matter that is witnessed to, and made them a proof against whoever denies this testimony, just as one takes clear evidence against whoever denies the truth. The proof was established through the Messengers over creation, and these are the deputies of the Messengers and their successors in establishing God's proofs over His servants.

[Section: Explanation of the testimony of those possessed of knowledge]

The testimony of those possessed of knowledge has been interpreted as affirmation (iqrar), and it has been interpreted as clarification and manifestation (tabyin and izhar).

The correct view is that it includes both matters: their testimony is affirmation, manifestation, and proclamation, and they are God's witnesses over mankind on the Day of Resurrection. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿He named you Muslims before, and in this, that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Hajj: 78].

So He informed that He made them upright and excellent, and He praised them by mentioning them before He brought them into being, because it had preceded in His knowledge that He would take them as witnesses bearing witness over the nations on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever does not uphold this testimony – in knowledge and action, in recognition and affirmation, in calling and teaching, and in guidance – is not among God's witnesses. And God is the One sought for help.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 3, verse 19:**

"Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam" (﴿إنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الإسْلامُ﴾).

The exegetes (*mufassirun*) differed over whether this is a new, independent statement or is included within the content of this testimony, in which case it is part of what is witnessed to.

This disagreement is based on the two readings of the *inna* in ﴿إنَّ﴾, with a kasra (إنَّ) or a fatha (أنَّ). Most readers read it with a kasra, as a new sentence (*istinaf*, a resumptive or independent clause). Al-Kisa'i alone read it with a fatha. The stronger view is the kasra, because the preceding speech is complete, so the second clause confirms and emphasizes the content of what came before. This is more emphatic in affirmation and more fitting in praise and commendation. For this reason the kasra in ﴿إنّا كُنّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ إنَّهُ هو البَرُّ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [al-Tur: 28] is better than the fatha. Likewise, the kasra in the words of the one saying the talbiyah, "Here I am, O Allah, indeed the praise and the blessing are Yours," is better than the fatha.

Three explanations have been given for the reading of al-Kisa'i:

The first is that the testimony falls on both clauses, so that ﴿إنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الإسْلامُ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19] is part of what is witnessed to. In this case the fatha of *anna* in ﴿أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلّا هُوَ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18] is understood as dropping the preposition, meaning "that there is no god but He." This is the explanation of al-Farra', and it is very weak, because the meaning goes against it. What is witnessed to is the very statement "that there is no god but He." So what is witnessed to is *anna* and what falls within its scope, and the attention and the purpose were directed to this and achieved through it. Nevertheless, this view, despite its weakness, has a sound sense, which is that the meaning is: Allah bore witness to His Oneness, that the religion with Allah is Islam, and Islam is His Oneness (*tawhid*), glorified is He. Thus the testimony includes His Oneness and the confirmation of His religion, that it is Islam and nothing other than it.

The second explanation is that the testimony falls on both clauses together, both being witnessed to, with the conjunction *wa* (and) omitted but intended. The sense is: "and that the religion with Allah is Islam." In this case the sentence dispenses with the conjunction because the preceding item it refers back to is mentioned. This is like the omission of the conjunction in ﴿ثَلاثَةٌ رابِعُهم كَلْبُهم ويَقُولُونَ خَمْسَةٌ سادِسُهم كَلْبُهُمْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 22]. Mentioning the *wa* and omitting it are both fine, as it is omitted here and mentioned in ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَبْعَةٌ وثامِنُهم كَلْبُهُمْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 22].

The third explanation, which is the view of the Basrians (*al-Basriyyun*), is to make the second *anna* a *badal* (substitute, apposition) of the first. The sense is: "Allah bore witness that the religion with Allah is Islam." The words ﴿أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلّا هُوَ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18] serve as a preparation (*tawti'a*) and introduction to the second clause. This is a *badal* in which the second is the same as the first, since the religion, which is Islam itself, with Allah is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and the upholding of its right. You may also take it, in this view, as a *badal al-ishtimal* (a substitute of inclusion), because Islam includes *tawhid*.

If it is said: "On this reading it should have been said, 'Indeed the religion with Allah is Islam,' since the meaning is: 'Allah bore witness that the religion with Him is Islam.' Why did it shift to the explicit noun?"

It is said: This supports the reading of the majority and shows that it is more eloquent and better. However, it is permissible to put the explicit noun in place of the pronoun, and this occurs often in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ واعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ العِقابِ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 196] And He said: ﴿واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [al-Anfal: 69] And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿والَّذِينَ يُمَسِّكُونَ بِالكِتابِ وأقامُوا الصَّلاةَ إنّا لا نُضِيعُ أجْرَ المُصْلِحِينَ﴾ [al-A'raf: 170]

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The polytheists boasted of their forefathers, and each group said, 'There is no religion except the religion of our fathers and what they were upon.' So Allah, exalted is He, refuted them, saying: ﴿إنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الإسْلامُ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19], meaning the one brought by Muhammad (ﷺ), which is the religion of the prophets from first to last. Allah has no religion other than it." ﴿وَمَن يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الإسْلامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنهُ وهو في الآخِرَةِ مِنَ الخاسِرِينَ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 85]

The statement ﴿إنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الإسْلامُ﴾ indicates that it is the religion of all His prophets, messengers and followers, from first to last, and that Allah never had, and never will have, any religion other than it. The first of the messengers, Noah, said: ﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَما سَألْتُكم مِن أجْرٍ إنْ أجْرِيَ إلّا عَلى اللَّهِ وأُمِرْتُ أنْ أكُونَ مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ﴾ [Yunus: 72] Abraham and Isma'il said: ﴿رَبَّنا واجْعَلْنا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِنا أُمَّةً مُسْلِمَةً لَكَ - ووَصّى بِها إبْراهِيمُ بَنِيهِ ويَعْقُوبُ يابَنِيَّ إنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفى لَكُمُ الدِّينَ فَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إلّا وأنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 128-132]

Ya'qub said to his sons at death: ﴿ما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن بَعْدِي قالُوا نَعْبُدُ إلَهَكَ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133] up to His words ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133]

Musa said to his people: ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنتُمْ بِاللَّهِ فَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلُوا إنْ كُنْتُمْ مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ [Yunus: 84]

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿فَلَمّا أحَسَّ عِيسى مِنهُمُ الكُفْرَ قالَ مَن أنْصارِي إلى اللَّهِ قالَ الحَوارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أنْصارُ اللَّهِ آمَنّا بِاللَّهِ واشْهَدْ بِأنّا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ [Al 'Imran: 52]

The Queen of Sheba said: ﴿رَبِّ إنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي وأسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمانَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Naml: 44]

Thus Islam is the religion of the people of the heavens and the religion of the people of monotheism (*tawhid*) among the people of the earth. Allah does not accept from anyone a religion other than it. The religions of the people of the earth are six: one belongs to the Compassionate (al-Rahman), and five belong to Satan. The religion of the Compassionate is Islam, and those belonging to Satan are Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism (*al-Majusiyyah*), Sabianism (*al-Sabi'ah*), and the religion of the polytheists.

This is some of what this great verse contains of the secrets of *tawhid* and of knowledge. Do not prolong the discussion of it, for it is more important than the discourse of the author of *al-Manazil*.

((Part Four))

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 3, verse 26 (part 1 of 3):

The verse begins with Him, glorified is He, affirming His sole sovereignty over all things, and that He alone is the One who bestows dominion upon whomever He wills and strips it from whomever He wills, and no other. The first points to His exclusive possession of sovereignty, and the second to His exclusive disposal of it. He, glorified is He, is the One who grants honour to whomever He wills, in whatever forms of honour He wills, and humbles whomever He wills by stripping that honour from him, and all good is in His hand, and no one has any share of it alongside Him. Then He concluded it with His saying: ﴿Indeed You are Powerful over all things﴾.

The verse thus encompasses His sole dominion, His disposal of it, and the comprehensiveness of His power, and it includes that all these acts are in His hand and that all of them are good. Thus His stripping dominion from whomever He wills and His humiliating whomever He wills is good, even if it is evil relative to the one stripped and humbled. For this disposal revolves between justice, bounty, wisdom and benefit, and does not depart from these. All of this is good, for which the Lord is praised and extolled, just as He is praised and extolled for His being exalted above evil and that it does not belong to Him. As is established in Sahih Muslim, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to extol his Lord with this in the opening supplication, in his saying:

"Here I am at Your service, and at Your pleasure. All good is in Your hands, and evil does not come from You. I am by You and to You. Blessed are You and exalted."

So He is exalted above being attributed with evil. Rather, everything attributed to Him is good, and evil only becomes evil by its being cut off from being attributed and related to Him. Had it been attributed to Him, it would not be evil, as its explanation will come. He, glorified is He, is the Creator of good and evil, so evil is in some of His creatures, not in His creation and act. His creation, His act, His decree and His predestination are all good. For this reason He, glorified is He, is exempt from injustice, which in reality is placing a thing in other than its place, as has preceded. He places things only in their fitting places, and that is all good, while evil is placing a thing in other than its proper place. So if it is placed in its place, it is not evil. Thus it is known that evil does not belong to Him, and His Most Beautiful Names bear witness to this. Among them are al-Quddus (the Holy), al-Salam (the Source of Peace), al-'Aziz (the Mighty), al-Jabbar (the Compeller), al-Mutakabbir (the Supreme). Al-Quddus is the One exalted above every evil, deficiency and defect, as the people of tafsir said: He is the One pure from every defect, exalted above what does not befit Him. This is the saying of the people of language, and the root of the word is purity and transcendence. From it comes Bayt al-Maqdis, because it is a place where one is purified of sins, and whoever his mother bore him intending only to pray there returns from his sin as on the day his mother bore him. From it the Garden is called hazirat al-quds, for its purity from the afflictions of this world. From it Jibril is called Ruh al-Quds, because he is pure from every defect.

From it is the saying of the angels: ﴿and we glorify You and sanctify You﴾.

It was said that the meaning is "and we sanctify ourselves for You," so it is construed with the lam, and this is nothing. The correct view is that the meaning is "we sanctify You and exalt You above what does not befit You," and this is the saying of the majority of the people of tafsir.

Ibn Jarir said: "'And we sanctify You' means we ascribe to You what is among Your attributes of purity from defilements, and from what the disbelievers attribute to You." He said: Some of them said: "we magnify You and glorify You," related by Abu Salih.

Mujahid said: "we magnify You and exalt You," end of quote.

Some of them said: we exalt You above evil, so we do not attribute it to You, and the lam in it is according to its usage in His saying: ﴿radifa lakum﴾, because the meaning is the glorification of Allah, not the glorification of their souls for His sake.

I say: For this reason this word is joined with their saying ﴿we glorify You with Your praise﴾, for tasbih is the exaltation of Allah, glorified is He, above every evil.

Maymun ibn Mihran said: "Subhan Allah is a word by which the Lord is magnified and by which He is exempted from evil."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is an exaltation of Allah from every evil." The root of the word is distancing, from the saying "sabahtu fi al-ardi" when one travels far in the land, and from it: "each in an orbit they swim" (yasbahun). Whoever praises Allah and exalts Him above evil has glorified Him. It is said: "sabbaha Allah" and "sabbaha lahu," and "qaddasahu" and "qaddasa lahu." Likewise His name al-Salam, for He is the One who is free from defects and deficiencies. To describe Him with al-Salam is more emphatic in this than to describe Him as "the one who is safe." Among the requirements of describing Him with this is that His creation is safe from His injustice to them. So He, glorified is He, is free from the will of injustice and evil, and from naming it after Him, and from His act, and from attributing it to Him. He is al-Salam, free from attributes of deficiency, acts of deficiency and names of deficiency, safeguarding His creation from injustice. For this reason He, glorified is He, described the Night of Decree as "peace," and the Garden as "the abode of peace," and the greeting of its people is "peace," and He praised His friends with "the word of peace." All of this is of the One free from defects. Likewise al-Kabir is among His names, and al-Mutakabbir.

Qatadah said: "and other than him: He is the One who is exalted above evil."

He also said: "The One who is exalted above evil deeds."

Muqatil said: "The One magnified above every evil."
