[Section on some of the wisdoms and praiseworthy aims that were in the battle of Uhud]

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has indicated its foundations and principles in Surat Al 'Imran, where He opened the account with His saying: ﴿And when you went out early from your family to station the believers at their positions for battle﴾ [Al 'Imran: 121], through to the completion of sixty verses.

Among them: making them aware of the evil consequence of disobedience, cowardice and disputing, and that what befell them was only due to the ill effect of that, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He showed you that which you love. Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you; but He has pardoned you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152].

When they tasted the consequence of their disobedience of the Messenger, their disputing and their cowardice, they became afterwards more cautious, more watchful, and more guarded against the causes of abandonment.

Among them: that the wisdom and sunnah of Allah regarding His messengers and their followers is that they are sometimes granted victory and sometimes overcome, but the final outcome is theirs. For if they were always victorious, the believers and others would have entered among them, and the truthful would not have been distinguished from others; and if they were always defeated, the purpose of the mission and message would not have been achieved. So the wisdom of Allah required that He combine both for them, so that those who follow them and obey them for the truth would be distinguished from those who follow them only for dominance and victory.

Among them: that this is among the signs of the messengers, as Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan: "Did you fight him?" He said: "Yes." He said: "How is the war between you and him?" He said: "It is a series of exchanges: he gains against us one time, and we gain against him another time." He said: "Thus are the messengers tried, and then the final outcome is theirs."

Among them: that the true believer be distinguished from the lying hypocrite. When Allah granted the Muslims victory over their enemies on the Day of Badr, and their fame spread, some who were not inwardly with them entered Islam outwardly. So the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, required that He cause His servants an ordeal that distinguished the believer from the hypocrite. The hypocrites raised their heads in this expedition, spoke what they had been concealing, their hidden things became manifest, their allusions became explicit, and people divided into disbeliever, believer and hypocrite in an evident division. The believers knew that they had an enemy within their own homes who was always with them, so they prepared against them and guarded themselves from them. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. And Allah would not give you knowledge of the unseen, but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran: 179].

That is, Allah would not leave you in the state you are in, of the believers being mixed with the hypocrites, until He distinguishes the people of faith from the people of hypocrisy, as He distinguished them by the ordeal on the Day of Uhud. ﴿Nor would Allah give you knowledge of the unseen﴾ by which He distinguishes between these and those, for they are distinguished in His unseen and knowledge, and He, glory be to Him, wills to distinguish them with a visible distinction, so that what is known to Him, which is unseen, becomes witnessed. His saying: ﴿But Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills﴾ is an exception to what He negated regarding the creatures' knowledge of the unseen apart from the messengers, for He informs them of whatever He wills of His unseen, as He said: ﴿The Knower of the unseen; He does not reveal His unseen to anyone except those whom He has approved of the messengers﴾ [Al-Jinn: 26-27]. So your portion and your happiness lie in belief in the unseen which He reveals to His messengers; if you believe in it and are certain of it, then for you is the greatest reward and honor.

Among them: the drawing out of the servanthood of His allies and party in times of ease and hardship, in what they love and what they dislike, and in the state of their victory and their enemies' victory over them. When they remain steadfast in obedience and servanthood in what they love and what they dislike, they are truly His servants, unlike one who worships Allah on a single edge, only in ease, blessing and well-being.

Among them: that if He, glory be to Him, granted them victory always, gave them triumph over their enemy in every place, and established for them firm power and domination over their enemies forever, their souls would transgress, become haughty and exalted. Had He extended to them victory and triumph, they would be in the state they would be in if He had extended provision to them. Nothing reforms His servants except ease and hardship, strength and gentleness, contraction and expansion. He is the Manager of His servants' affairs as befits His wisdom; indeed He is All-Aware, All-Seeing of them.

Among them: that when He tests them with being overcome, defeat and rout, they become humbled, broken and submissive, and so they deserve from Him might and victory, for the robe of victory is only bestowed together with the mantle of humiliation and brokenness. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were humble﴾ [Al 'Imran: 123].

And He said: ﴿And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it availed you nothing﴾ [al-Tawba: 25]. So when He, glory be to Him, wills to honor His servant, to console him and to give him victory, He first breaks him, and His consolation and victory for him are in proportion to his humiliation and brokenness.

Among them: that He, glory be to Him, prepared for His believing servants stations in the abode of His honor which their deeds could not reach, and they could not attain them except through trial and ordeal. So He facilitated for them the means that lead them to them, through His tribulation and testing, just as He enabled them to do the righteous deeds which are among the means of arriving at them.

Among them: that souls acquire, from constant well-being, victory and wealth, transgression and inclination toward the immediate world, and that is a sickness that hinders them from earnestness in their journey to Allah and the Hereafter. When their Lord, Owner and Merciful wills honor for them, He appoints for them trials and tests that serve as a remedy for that sickness that hinders the swift journey toward Him. That trial and ordeal are like a physician who gives the patient a bitter medicine and cuts out painful veins to extract the diseases from him; were he to leave him, the diseases would overcome him until his ruin would come through them.

Among them: that martyrdom is, in His sight, among the highest ranks of His allies, and the martyrs are His elect and the closest of His servants. There is no rank beyond that of the truthful (siddiqiyya) except martyrdom. He, glory be to Him, loves to take from among His servants martyrs whose blood is shed in His love and pleasure, who prefer His good pleasure and what He loves over their own souls. There is no way to attain this rank except by ordaining the causes that lead to it, such as the enemy being given power over them.

Among them: when Allah, glory be to Him, wishes to destroy His enemies and wipe them out, He предестines for them the causes that merit their destruction and annihilation. Among the greatest of these, after their disbelief, are their rebellion and transgression, their extreme harm to His allies, and their fighting against them and their domination over them. Through this, His allies are purified of their sins and faults, and His enemies increase in the causes of their annihilation and ruin. Glory be to Him and exalted is He, has mentioned this in His saying: ﴿So do not weaken, nor grieve, and you will be superior if you are believers. If a wound has touched you, a similar wound has touched the people. And these days We alternate among the people, so that Allah may know those who believe and take from among you martyrs. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers. And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 139-141]. In this address He combined encouraging them, strengthening their souls, reviving their resolve and aspirations, with good consolation and the mention of the dazzling wisdoms that required the disbelievers to gain the upper hand over them. So He said: ﴿If a wound has touched you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾ [Al 'Imran: 140]. You are thus equal in wounds and pain, but you differ in hope and reward, as He said: ﴿If you suffer pain, they suffer pain as you suffer, but you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾ [An-Nisa: 104]. So what is wrong with you that you weaken and falter at the wound and pain? That has befallen them in the way of Satan, while you have been struck in My way and in seeking My pleasure.

Then He informed that He alternates the days of this worldly life among the people, and that they are a present passing condition, which He divides into turns between His allies and His enemies, unlike the Hereafter, whose might, victory and hope are purely for those who believe.

Then He mentioned another wisdom, which is that the believers be distinguished from the hypocrites. He knows them with knowledge of seeing and witnessing, after they had been known in His unseen knowledge. That unseen knowledge does not entail reward or punishment; rather, reward and punishment are entailed only upon what is known once it becomes witnessed and actual in the senses.

Then He mentioned another wisdom, which is His taking martyrs from among them. He loves martyrs among His servants, and has prepared for them the highest and best of ranks, and has taken them for Himself, so He must grant them the degree of martyrdom.

His saying: ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 140] is a very subtly placed alert to His dislike and hatred of the hypocrites who withdrew from His Prophet on the day of Uhud and so did not witness it, and whom He did not take as martyrs, because He did not love them. So He turned them back and sent them away, to deprive them of what He had specially granted to the believers on that day and what He gave to those who were martyred from among them. Thus He held back these wrongdoers from the causes with which He granted success to His allies and His party.

Then He mentioned another wisdom in what befell them that day, which is the purification of those who believe, that is, cleansing them and freeing them from sins and from the afflictions of the souls. Also, He purified and separated them from the hypocrites, so they were distinguished from them. Thus two purifications were achieved for them: a purification from their own souls, and a purification from those who used to show that they were among them while they were in fact their enemy.

Then He mentioned another wisdom, which is the destruction of the disbelievers through their tyranny, transgression and aggression. Then He denounced their reckoning and their assumption that they would enter Paradise without striving in His way and enduring the harm of His enemies. This is impossible, so whoever assumes and reckons it is denounced.

So He said: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove and known the patient?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 142], meaning: and this has not yet occurred from you, so He knows it. For if it had occurred, He would have known it and rewarded you with Paradise, so the reward is for what actually occurs and is known, not for mere knowledge, since Allah does not reward a servant for His mere knowledge of him unless what is known of him occurs. Then He rebuked them for their defeat over a matter they used to wish for and desire to meet.

So He said: ﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you met it. Now you have seen it while you were looking on﴾ [Al 'Imran: 143].

Ibn 'Abbas said: When Allah informed them through His Prophet of the honour He bestowed upon the martyrs of Badr, they desired martyrdom and wished for a battle in which they might be martyred and join their brothers. So Allah showed them that on the day of Uhud and caused it for them, but they did not last long before they fled, except for those whom Allah willed. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you met it. Now you have seen it while you were looking on﴾.

Another wisdom: the battle of Uhud was a prelude and a sign before the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So He made them firm and rebuked them for turning back on their heels should the Messenger of Allah ﷺ die or be killed. Rather, what is obligatory for them toward him is to remain steadfast upon his religion and his monotheism, and to die upon it or be killed. For they worship only the Lord of Muhammad, who is living and does not die. If Muhammad dies or is killed, it is not fitting that this should turn them away from his religion and what he brought. ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾, and Muhammad ﷺ was not sent to be made immortal, neither he nor they, but so that they might die upon Islam and monotheism, for death is inevitable whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dies or remains. For this reason He rebuked them for the return of those among them who turned back from their religion when Satan shouted that Muhammad had been killed. So He said: ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger, before whom messengers have passed away. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful﴾ [Al 'Imran: 144]. The grateful are those who recognised the value of the blessing and remained steadfast upon it until they died or were killed. So the effect of this reproach and the ruling of this address became manifest on the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died: those who turned back on their heels apostatised, while the grateful held firm to their religion. So Allah helped them, gave them might, granted them victory over their enemies, and made the final outcome theirs.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, informed that He has appointed for every soul a term that it must complete, after which it will be reached. Thus all people come to the watering-place of deaths as one arrival, though its causes vary, and they depart from the standing place of the Resurrection in different directions: a group in Paradise, and a group in the Blaze.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, informed that many multitudes of His prophets were killed, and many followers were killed with them. Those who remained did not weaken because of what afflicted them in His way, nor did they become feeble, nor did they submit, nor did they falter at the killing. Rather, they met martyrdom with strength, resolve and advance. They were not martyred retreating, submissive and humiliated, but were martyred honoured, noble, advancing and not turning back. The correct view is that the verse encompasses both groups.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, informed of what the prophets and their nations sought help with against their peoples: confession, repentance, seeking forgiveness, and asking their Lord to make their feet firm and to grant them victory over their enemies. So He said: ﴿And their saying was only that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affair, make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people." So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the good-doers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 147].

When the people knew that the enemy is only given power over them because of their sins, and that Satan only makes them slip and defeats them through them, and that these sins are of two kinds, either a shortcoming in a right or a transgression of a limit, and that victory is tied to obedience, they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affair." Then they knew that their Lord, blessed and exalted, if He does not make their feet firm and grant them victory, they would not be able to make their own feet firm or give their souls victory over their enemies. So they asked Him for what they knew was in His hand alone, and that if He did not make their feet firm and grant them victory, they would neither remain firm nor be victorious. Thus they fulfilled both stations: the station of the cause, which is monotheism and seeking refuge in Him, glory be to Him, and the station of removing the impediment to victory, which is sins and excess. Then Allah, glory be to Him, warned them against obeying their enemy, and informed that if they obeyed them they would lose this world and the Hereafter. In this there is an allusion to the hypocrites who obeyed the polytheists when they gained the upper hand and were victorious on the day of Uhud.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, informed that He is the Protector of the believers, and He is the best of helpers, so whoever He takes as ally is the one who is helped.

Then He informed them that He would cast terror into the hearts of their enemies, which would prevent them from attacking them and from advancing to fight them, and that He strengthens His party with a host of terror by which they prevail over their enemies. That terror is because of the polytheism in their hearts, and the terror is in proportion to the polytheism. The one who associates partners with Allah is the most fearful and terrified of things, while those who believed and did not mix their faith with polytheism have security, guidance and success, and the polytheist has fear, misguidance and wretchedness.

Then He informed them that He fulfilled His promise to them of victory over their enemy, for He is the One who keeps promises. And that if they had persisted in obedience and adherence to the Messenger's command, their victory would have continued. But they stepped out of obedience and left their position, so they were stripped of the protection of obedience, and victory departed from them. So He turned them away from their enemy as a punishment and a trial, and to make them know the evil consequences of disobedience and the good outcome of obedience.

Then He informed that after all of this He pardoned them, and that He is full of bounty toward His believing servants. It was said to al-Hasan: "How can He pardon them when He gave their enemies power over them, until they killed whom they killed, mutilated them and inflicted upon them what they inflicted?" He said: "Had He not pardoned them, He would have uprooted them. But by His pardon toward them, He repelled their enemy from them after they had resolved to exterminate them."

Then He reminded them of their state at the time of fleeing, going upward, that is, hastening in flight and going off into the land, or climbing the mountain, not turning back for anyone, neither their prophet nor their companions, while the Messenger was calling them from behind: "To the servants of Allah! I am the Messenger of Allah!"

So He repaid them for this flight and retreat with grief upon grief: the grief of defeat and breaking, and the grief of Satan's shout among them that Muhammad had been killed.

It was also said: He repaid you with grief for the grief you caused His Messenger, by your fleeing from him and leaving him to his enemy. So the grief that befell you was a recompense for the grief you inflicted upon His Prophet. But the first view is more apparent, for several reasons:

First: His saying: ﴿So that you would not grieve over what escaped you or what afflicted you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 153] is an alert to the wisdom of this grief upon grief, which is that it makes them forget grief over what they had lost of victory and what afflicted them of defeat and wounds. Thus they forgot the cause, and this is achieved only through a grief that is followed by another grief.

Second: it corresponds to what actually happened. For they had the grief of the loss of the spoils, then the grief of defeat followed it, then the grief of the wounds that struck them, then the grief of the killing, then the grief of hearing that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been killed, then the grief of their enemies appearing on the mountain above them. The intended meaning is not just two griefs, but continuous grief to complete the trial and examination.

Third: His saying "with grief" is part of the reward, not that it is the cause of the reward. The meaning is: He rewarded you with grief following grief, as a recompense for your fleeing, your abandoning your Prophet ﷺ and his companions, your not responding to him while he was calling you, your opposing him by staying at your post, your disputing the matter and your cowardice. Each of these matters entails a grief particular to it, so griefs piled upon them as their causes and requirements piled up. Had He not overlooked them with His pardon, it would have been something else.

Among His gentleness, mercy, and compassion toward them is that these matters which proceeded from them were among the requirements of human nature, and they are among the remnants of the souls that prevent the lasting, steadfast victory. So through His gentleness He arranged for them causes that brought these tendencies from potential into actuality, and their harmful consequences followed. Then they knew that repentance from them, guarding against their like, and repelling them by their opposites was a necessary matter, and that success and lasting, steadfast victory would not be complete for them except through it. Thereafter they were far more cautious and more aware of the gates through which they had been struck.

"Perhaps bodies are healed by illnesses."

Then He, glory be to Him, made amends for them in His mercy, lightened that distress for them, and removed it from them through the drowsiness He sent down upon them as security and mercy from Him. Drowsiness in battle is a sign of victory and security, just as He sent it down upon them on the Day of Badr. He also informed that whoever is not overtaken by that drowsiness is one whom his own soul has concerned, not his religion, his Prophet, or his Companions, and that they "think about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah" (the age of ignorance before Islam).

This thought that is not fitting for Allah has been explained as: that He, glory be to Him, does not help His Messenger, that his affair will be extinguished, and that He will hand him over to be killed. It has also been explained as their thinking that what befell them was not by His decree and destiny, and that He had no wisdom in it. Thus it was interpreted as denying wisdom, denying divine decree, and denying that He would complete the affair of His Messenger and make him victorious over all religion. This is the evil thought that the hypocrites and the polytheists held about Him, glory be to Him and exalted, in Surah al-Fath (Surah 48), where He says: ﴿And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who think about Allah an evil thought. Upon them is a cycle of evil, and Allah is angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil is the destination﴾ [al-Fath: 6].

This was an evil thought and the thought of the Jahiliyyah, attributed to the people of ignorance, and a thought other than the truth, because it is a thought of what does not befit His beautiful names, His exalted attributes, and His essence, which is free of every defect and evil. It is contrary to what befits His wisdom, His praiseworthiness, His singularity in lordship and divinity, what befits His true promise that He does not break, His word that preceded for His messengers that He will help them and not forsake them, and for His army that they are the victorious ones. Whoever thinks that He will not help His Messenger, will not complete his affair, will not support him and support his party, will not exalt them and grant them victory over their enemies, will not make them prevail over them, that He will not help His religion and His Book, and that He will let polytheism prevail over monotheism and falsehood over truth with a lasting dominance, by which monotheism and truth will be extinguished in a way that never rises again, has thought an evil thought about Allah and attributed to Him what is contrary to His perfection, majesty, attributes, and qualities. For His praiseworthiness, His might, His wisdom, and His divinity reject that, and reject that His party and His army be humbled, or that lasting victory and constant triumph be for His enemies, the polytheists who associate others with Him and equate others with Him. Whoever thinks this about Him has not known Him, nor known His names, nor known His attributes and perfection. Likewise, whoever denies that this was by His decree and destiny has not known Him, nor known His lordship, His dominion, and His greatness. Likewise, whoever denies that He decreed that and other things for a profound wisdom and a praiseworthy end for which He deserves praise, and claims that it came only from a bare will devoid of wisdom and of a desired end that He loves more than its loss, and that the harmful causes which lead to it have a decree that does not go beyond wisdom because they lead to what He loves, even if they are disliked by Him, has not understood Him. He did not decree them in vain, nor create them without purpose, nor create them as falsehood. ﴿That is the thought of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad: 27]. Most people think about Allah other than the truth, an evil thought, regarding what concerns them and what He does to others. No one is spared from this except one who knows Allah, knows His names and attributes, and knows what His praise and wisdom require. Whoever despairs of His mercy and gives up hope of His comfort has thought an evil thought about Him.

Whoever holds that He would punish His friends despite their good deeds and sincerity, and would treat them the same as His enemies, has thought an evil thought about Him.

Whoever thinks that He would leave His creation purposeless, idle from command and prohibition, would not send His messengers to them, nor send down His Books to them, but would leave them neglected like livestock, has thought an evil thought about Him.

Whoever thinks that He would not gather His servants after their death for reward and punishment in an abode where He recompenses the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil, would not clarify for His creation the truth of what they differed about, would not show all the worlds His truthfulness and the truthfulness of His messengers and that His enemies were the liars, has thought an evil thought about Him.

Whoever thinks that He would waste for him the righteous deed he performed sincerely for His noble face in obedience to His command, and would nullify it for him without any cause from the servant, or that He would punish him for what he had no hand in, no choice, no power, and no will in bringing about, but would punish him for His own act through him, or thinks it permissible for Him to support His enemies who lie against Him with the miracles through which He supports His prophets and messengers, and to make them flow through their hands so that they lead His servants astray, and that everything is good for Him, even punishing one who spent his life in obeying Him by making him dwell eternally in the Hellfire at the lowest of the low, and bestowing blessings on one who spent his life in enmity toward Him, His messengers, and His religion, raising him to the highest of the high, and that both are equal in goodness for Him, and that the prohibition of one and the occurrence of the other is known only through a truthful report, since reason does not judge the ugliness of one and the goodness of the other, has thought an evil thought about Him.

In sum, whoever thinks about Him what is contrary to what He described Himself with and what His messengers described Him with, or nullifies the realities of what He described Himself with and what His messengers described Him with, has thought an evil thought about Him.

Whoever thinks that He has a son or a partner, or that anyone intercedes with Him without His permission, or that between Him and His creation there are intermediaries who carry their needs to Him, or that He has set up for His servants friends besides Him whom they draw near to through, seek means to Him through, and make intermediaries between themselves and Him, calling upon them, loving them as they love Him, fearing them, and hoping in them, has thought the worst and most evil thought about Him.

Whoever thinks that He grants what is with Him by disobedience to Him and opposition to Him just as one obtains it by obedience and drawing near to Him, has thought about Him what is contrary to His wisdom and to what His names and attributes require, and that is an evil thought.

Whoever thinks that if one leaves something for His sake, He will not compensate him with something better, or whoever does something for His sake, He will not give him something better than it, has thought an evil thought about Him.

Whoever thinks that He becomes angry with His servant, punishes him, and deprives him without any sin or cause from the servant, but only by mere will and pure volition, has thought an evil thought about Him.

Whoever thinks that if he is sincere to Him in desire and fear, humbles himself before Him, asks Him, seeks His help, and relies upon Him, He will disappoint him and not give him what he asked for, has thought an evil thought about Him, and has thought of Him what is not fitting for Him.

Whoever thinks that if one disobeys Him, He will reward him as He rewards one who obeys Him, and he asks Him for that in his supplication, has thought of Him what His wisdom and praiseworthiness do not require, what is not fitting for Him, and what He does not do.

Whoever thinks that if he angers and displeases Him, and persists in His disobedience, then takes a friend other than Him, and calls upon an angel or a living or dead human besides Him, hoping through that to benefit him with his Lord and deliver him from His punishment, has thought an evil thought about Him, and that increases his distance from Allah and his punishment.

Whoever thinks that He empowers His enemies over His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) with a lasting, continuous domination during his life and after his death, and tests him with them so that they never leave him, and that when he died they seized the affair without any testament, wronged the People of his House, deprived them of their right and humiliated them, and that might, victory, and dominion were always for his enemies and the enemies of his people, without any crime or sin on the part of his allies and the people of truth, while He sees their oppression of them, their seizure of their right, and their changing of the religion of their Prophet, and He is able to help His allies, party, and army but does not help them and does not make them prevail, but makes their enemies prevail over them forever. Or that He is not able to do that, but this happened without His power or will; then He made those who altered His religion his companions in his grave, while his community sends greetings upon him and upon them at every time, as the Rafidah (a Shiite sect) claim, has thought the worst and most evil thought about Him. Whether they say He is able to help them and grant them dominion and victory, or that He is not able to do so, they either impugn His power or His wisdom and praiseworthiness, and that is an evil thought about Him. There is no doubt that the Lord who did this is hateful to those who think it, and is not praiseworthy in their eyes, whereas it was obligatory that He do otherwise. But they patched up this corrupt thought with a greater tear, and sought refuge from the scorching sand in the fire. They said: this did not happen by the will of Allah, and He has no power to repel it and help His allies, for He does not have power over the acts of His servants, nor are those acts within His power. So they thought about Him the thought of their brothers, the Magians and the Dualists (Thanawiyya) regarding their lord, and of every falsifier, disbeliever, and humiliated, subdued innovator, who thinks this about his Lord, and that he is more deserving of victory, triumph, and exaltation than his adversaries. Most of creation, indeed all of them except whom Allah wills, think about Allah other than the truth, an evil thought. For most of the children of Adam believe that they are deprived of their rights and have less than their share, and that they deserve more than what Allah gave them, and the tongue of their state says: "My Lord wronged me and withheld from me what I deserve," and their souls bear witness to this, though with their tongues they deny it and do not dare to state it openly. Whoever searches his soul and penetrates into its hidden depths and secrets will see that this is latent within it, like the fire hidden in the tinder. Strike the tinder of whomever you wish, and its spark will reveal what is in its tinder. Had you searched whomever you searched, you would have found in him complaint against destiny, blame of it, and proposing to it what contradicts what has occurred, saying that it should have been thus and so; some feel self-sufficient and some regard their share as much. Examine yourself: are you safe from that?

"If you are saved from it, you are saved from a great matter; otherwise, I do not think you will be saved."

Therefore, let the intelligent person who counsels his own soul take heed of this point, repent to Allah, the Exalted, and seek His forgiveness at every time for his evil thought about his Lord. Let him think ill of his own soul, which is the abode of every evil and the source of every wrong, built upon ignorance and injustice. It is more deserving of evil thought than the wisest of judges, the most just of the just, and the most merciful of the merciful: the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy, to whom belong complete self-sufficiency, complete praise, and complete wisdom, who is exalted above every evil in His essence, attributes, acts, and names. His essence has absolute perfection from every aspect; His attributes are likewise; His acts are likewise. All of them are wisdom, benefit, mercy, and justice, and all His names are beautiful.

"So do not think about your Lord an evil thought, for Allah is more deserving of goodness."

And never think good of yourself:

"How can the oppressive, wrongdoing, ignorant one be trusted? Say, O soul, you are the abode of every evil."

"Can good be hoped for from a dead, miserly one? Think ill of yourself and you will find it so, and its good is like the impossible."

"And whatever piety or good is in you is not from yourself, but are gifts of the Majestic Lord. Be thankful to the Guide."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 3, verse 121 (part 4 of 4):

The purpose for which we were led into this discussion is His saying: ﴿And a group, their own selves had concerned them, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of ignorance﴾ [Al 'Imran: 154]. Then He informed of the statement that issued from their false thinking, which is their saying: ﴿Is there anything for us in the matter?﴾ and their saying: ﴿If there had been anything for us in the matter, we would not have been killed here﴾.

Their aim in the first and second statements was not to affirm divine decree (qadar) and to refer the whole matter to Allah. Had that been their aim in the first statement, they would not have been blamed for it, and the response to it would not have been fitting with His saying: ﴿Say, indeed the matter, all of it, belongs to Allah﴾.

Nor did the source of this statement come from the thought of ignorance (zann al-jahiliyyah). For this reason more than one of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: their false thinking here is the denial of divine decree (takdhib bil-qadar), and their thinking that if the matter had been in their hands, and if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions had followed them and listened to them, they would not have been struck by killing, and victory and triumph would have been theirs. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuted them in this false thinking, which is the thought of ignorance, the thought attributed to the people of ignorance who claim, after the decree and divine destiny have taken effect, which could not be otherwise, that they were able to repel it, and that if the matter had been in their hands, the decree would not have taken effect. Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿Say, indeed the matter, all of it, belongs to Allah﴾. So nothing happens except what His decree and destiny have preceded, and what His knowledge and His prior Book have run upon. What Allah wills occurs, without doubt, whether people wish it or refuse; and what He does not will does not occur, whether people will it or do not will it. What befell you of defeat and killing came by His universal command (al-amr al-kawni), which cannot be repelled, whether or not you had any part in the matter. And had you been in your houses, and killing had been written upon some of you, those upon whom killing was written would have gone out from their houses to their resting places, without doubt, whether or not they had any part in the matter. This is among the clearest refutations of the saying of the Qadariyyah, the deniers (al-nufat), who permit that something occurs which Allah does not will, and that He wills something which does not occur.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on surah 3, verse 123:

It is permissible that His saying ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾ be the reason (ta'lil) for His decreeing victory for them, for His commanding them to be mindful of God (taqwa), or for both together, and this is the apparent meaning.

So gratitude is the ultimate purpose of the creation and of the command.

(Benefit)

Among the points concerning the People of Badr is that they are, in general, better than others, but the individuals among them are not to be preferred over others, because there may be among others someone better than any individual among them, as the Prophet ﷺ said:

"The best of you is my generation (al-qarn), then those who follow them, then those who follow them."

So he distinguished between generations in general, because within the preference of one generation there may be someone better than him from another. For this reason it is known that Ahmad (ibn Hanbal) is better than Yazid, and Yazid lived in the era of the Successors (al-tabi'un), due to what occurred from Yazid that led to criticism of his integrity (adalah).

Riba (usury, the unlawful increase on loans) is of two kinds: the manifest (jali) and the hidden (khafi). The manifest kind was prohibited because of the great harm it contains, and the hidden kind was prohibited because it is a means (dhari'ah, a means leading to a prohibited end) to the manifest kind. So the prohibition of the first is intended directly, and the prohibition of the second is as a means. As for the manifest kind, it is riba al-nasi'ah (riba of deferment), which is what they used to practise in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance). It is like a man postponing his debt and adding to its amount; every time he postpones it, the amount increases, until a hundred becomes thousands upon thousands. Generally, only one who is destitute and in need does this. When the creditor sees that the one owed is postponing his demand and is patient with him in return for an increase he offers him, the debtor takes on the burden of paying it in order to ransom himself from the pressure of demand and imprisonment, and to hold off his creditor from time to time. Thus his harm intensifies, his calamity grows, and the debt overwhelms him until it consumes all that he possesses. Wealth then grows for the one in need without any benefit reaching him, and the usurer's wealth increases without any benefit coming from him to his brother, so he devours his brother's wealth falsely, and his brother suffers the utmost harm. Out of the mercy of the Most Merciful of the merciful, His wisdom, and His kindness to His creation, He prohibited riba, cursed the one who consumes it, the one who pays it, its scribe, and its two witnesses, and declared war from Him and from His Messenger upon whoever does not abandon it. No such threat has come for any other major sin, and for this reason it is among the greatest of the major sins.

Imam Ahmad was asked about the riba about which there is no doubt, and he said: it is that a man has a debt and says to him, "Will you pay, or will you increase it?" If he does not pay, he increases the amount for him and he increases the term for him. Allah, glorified is He, has made riba the opposite of charity (sadaqah), so the usurer is the opposite of the one who gives charity. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah destroys riba and makes charities grow﴾ [al-Baqarah: 276], and He said: ﴿And whatever you give in riba so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah; but whatever you give in zakah, seeking the Face of Allah — those are the ones who multiply﴾ [al-Rum: 39], and He said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume riba, doubled and multiplied, and fear Allah that you may be successful (130). And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers (131)﴾.

Then He mentioned the Garden which has been prepared for the righteous who spend in ease and in hardship, and these are the opposite of the usurers. So He, glorified is He, forbade riba, which is injustice toward people, and commanded charity, which is kindness toward them.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, from Usamah ibn Zayd, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Riba is only in deferment (nasi'ah)." Such a statement is intended to restrict perfection: that complete riba is only in deferment, just as the Exalted said: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely﴾ [al-Anfal: 2], up to His saying: ﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾ [al-Anfal: 4]. And like the saying of Ibn Mas'ud: "The scholar is only the one who fears Allah."

As for riba al-fadl (riba of excess), its prohibition is by way of blocking the means (sadd al-dhara'i'), as he clearly stated in the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Do not sell a dirham for two dirhams, for I fear for you al-Rima'," and al-Rima' is riba. He thus forbade them from riba al-fadl because of what he feared for them of riba al-nasi'ah. That is because when they sell a dirham for two dirhams, this is only done for the difference between the two types — whether in quality, in minting, in weight and lightness, or otherwise — and they gradually move from the immediate profit in it to the deferred profit, which is the very same as riba al-nasi'ah. This is a very close means, so out of the wisdom of the Lawgiver He blocked this means for them, and forbade them from selling a dirham for two dirhams, whether in cash or on credit. This is a wisdom that is rationally comprehensible and in accord with sound reason, and it closes for them the door to corruption.

Meaning: Indeed, there were nations before you, like you. So look at the evil end of those who denied, and know that the cause of that was their denial of the signs of Allah and His messengers. They are the root, and you are the branch; the common cause ('illah jami'ah) is denial, and the ruling is destruction.

Honour and exaltation belong only to the people of faith (al-iman) with which God sent His messengers and revealed His books. This faith is knowledge, action and state (hal). God the Exalted said: ﴿And you will be superior if you are believers.﴾

So the servant's share of exaltation is in proportion to the faith he has. God the Exalted said: ﴿Honour belongs to God, to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8].

So his share of honour is in proportion to the faith he has and its realities. If he misses a portion of exaltation and honour, then it corresponds to what he has missed of the realities of faith, in knowledge and in action, outwardly and inwardly.

Likewise, God's defence of the servant is in proportion to his faith. God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, God defends those who have believed﴾ [al-Hajj: 38].

So if the defence afforded to him is weak, it is due to the deficiency in his faith.

Likewise, sufficiency and being enough (al-hasb) are in proportion to faith. God the Exalted said: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you﴾ [al-Anfal: 64].

That is: God is sufficient for you and sufficient for your followers, i.e., He suffices you and suffices them. His sufficiency for them is in proportion to their following of His Messenger, their submission to him, and their obedience to him. Whatever is lacking of faith, the lack of all that returns to them.

The doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah) is that faith increases and decreases.

Likewise, God the Exalted's guardianship (wilayah) over His servant is in proportion to his faith. God the Exalted said: ﴿And God is the Protector of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 68], and God the Exalted said: ﴿God is the Protector of those who have believed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257].

Likewise, His special companionship (ma'iyyah khassah) is for the people of faith, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, God is with the believers﴾ [al-Anfal: 19].

So when faith decreases and weakens, the servant's share of God's guardianship over him and His special companionship is according to his share of faith.

Likewise, victory and complete support belong only to those of complete faith. God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believed in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir: 51], and He said: ﴿So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾ [al-Saff: 14].

Whoever's faith is deficient, his share of victory and support is diminished. Therefore, when a servant is afflicted with a calamity in himself or his wealth, or when his enemy is given power over him, it is only because of his sins, either by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act, and this is from the deficiency of his faith.

By this, the difficulty that many people raise regarding God's words ﴿And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [al-Nisa': 141] is resolved.

Many of them answer it by saying that He will not give them a way over them in the Hereafter, and others answer that He will not give them a way over them in argument.

The verified position is that such verses and the like, and the absence of a way (sabil) for the disbelievers over the people of complete faith, mean that when faith weakens, their enemy gains a way over them in proportion to what they have lost of their faith. They have given them a way over themselves by what they abandoned of obedience to God the Exalted.

So the believer is mighty, victorious, supported, sufficed, and defended by his very essence wherever he is, even if all the people of the earth gather against him, provided he upholds the reality of faith and its obligations, outwardly and inwardly.

God the Exalted has said to the believers: ﴿And do not weaken or grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 139], and God the Exalted said: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are superior, and God is with you and will not deprive you of your deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 35].

This guarantee is only through their faith and their deeds, which are among the soldiers of God, by which He protects them. He does not separate them from these deeds or cut them off from them, thereby nullifying them for them, just as He nullifies the deeds of the disbelievers and the hypocrites when they were for other than Him and did not conform to His command.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 3, verse 144:**

A man from the Muhajirun passed by a man from the Ansar who was writhing in his blood, and he said: "O so-and-so, did you know that Muhammad has been killed?"

The Ansari replied: "If Muhammad has been killed, he has indeed conveyed the message. So fight for your religion." Then this was revealed: ﴿Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have passed away before him﴾, and the verse continues.

Anas ibn al-Nadr came upon Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talhah ibn Ubaid Allah, along with men from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who had laid down their arms. He said: "What makes you sit idle?" They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been killed." He said: "What will you do with life after him? Rise and die in the same cause for which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died." Then he faced the enemy and fought until he was killed.

When Malik, the father of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, sucked the wound of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he cleaned it, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Spit it out." He said: "By Allah, I will never spit it out." Then he turned away. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to look at a man of the people of Paradise, let him look at this man."

Zayd ibn Thabit said: On the day of Uhud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to look for Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'. He said to me: "If you see him, convey my greetings to him and say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) says to you, 'How are you?'" So I went around among the slain until I came to him, and he was at his last breath, having seventy wounds, from spear thrusts, sword strikes and arrow shots. I said: "O Sa'd, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sends you his greetings and says to you: Tell me how you are." He said: "And upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) be peace. Say to him: O Messenger of Allah, I smell the fragrance of Paradise. And say to my people, the Ansar: You have no excuse before Allah if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is reached while there is a single eye among you that blinks." And his soul departed at that very moment.

Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram said: Before Uhud, I saw in a dream Mubashshir ibn Abd al-Mundhir, who said to me: "You will come to us in a few days." I said: "And where are you?" He said: "In Paradise, we roam in it as we wish." I said to him: "Were you not killed on the day of Badr?" He said: "Yes, then I was brought back to life." He mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "That is martyrdom, O Abu Jabir."

**(Benefit)**

After the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) entered upon Umm Ayman (Barakah the Abyssinian) while she was weeping. They said: "O Umm Ayman, what makes you weep? What Allah has is better for His Messenger."

She said: "I know that what Allah has is better for His Messenger. But I weep only because the news from heaven has ceased." Her words moved them both, and they wept.

**[Section]**

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us from his father, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken in death, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O people, if Muhammad was your god whom you worshipped, then your god has died. But if your God is Allah, who is in heaven, then your God has not died." Then he recited: ﴿Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have passed away before him﴾, until he finished the verse.

Al-Bukhari said in his Tarikh (al-Tarikh al-Kabir): Muhammad ibn Fudayl said, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken in death, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon him, bent over him, kissed his forehead, and said: "May my father and mother be your ransom. You were good in life and in death." And he said: "Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died. But whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is alive in heaven and does not die."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to the Banu Amr ibn Awf to reconcile between them, and the time of prayer came. The muezzin came to Abu Bakr, and he mentioned the hadith, in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured to Abu Bakr to remain in his place. Abu Bakr raised his hands and praised Allah for what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded him, then stepped back... and he mentioned it.

If you say: Almighty God has said, "And their only words were: Our Lord, forgive us our sins" (3:147), and in Surah al-Saff, "He will forgive you your sins" (61:12). What is the wisdom in omitting it here, and what is the difference?

I say: This is a report about the believers who had already been rescued from the sins of disbelief through their faith, and then were promised, for their striving in jihad, forgiveness of the sins they had committed during Islam, which are not destructive in the way that disbelief is destructive to the disbeliever. Thus forgiveness does not carry the meaning of rescue (istinqadh), since there is no encompassing of the sinner by sin. Rather, it carries the meaning of removal and nullification of sins, because good deeds remove bad deeds. This differs from the two previous verses, which are addressed to the polytheists and command them to do what will rescue and free them from the sins that encompass them, which is disbelief. Within that is the notification and indication that they are falling into a ruin that has encompassed them, and that nothing will rescue them from it except forgiveness, which includes rescue, a more specific meaning than nullification and removal. As for the believers, they have already been rescued.

As for His saying, "And He will remove from you some of your bad deeds" (3:... / 5:12 context), the "min" there is the partitive min (min al-tab'id), because the verse is in the context of the reward for charity. He said, "If you disclose your charities, it is good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, and He will remove from you some of your bad deeds." Charity does not remove all sins. Of this type is his saying ﷺ: "Let him expiate for his oath and let him do what is better."

Narrated by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, and al-Bukhari has something similar.

So he introduced "'an" into the sentence to signal the meaning of departing from the oath, since he mentioned the agent, who is the one departing. It is as if he said: "let him depart from his oath by expiation."

And since he did not mention the agent who expiates in His saying, "That is the expiation of your oaths" (5:89), and did not mention "min," and attributed the expiation to the oaths, this is an idafa of the verbal noun to its object, even though oaths do not themselves get expiated; rather, what is expiated is the breaking and the sin. But expiation is a release of the binding of the oath, so for this reason it is attributed to the oath, just as release is attributed to a binding, since the oath is a binding and expiation is its release. And God knows best.

**(Section)**

God, glory be to Him, placed enmity between Satan and the angel (al-Malak), between the intellect ('aql) and desire (hawa), and between the commanding self (al-nafs al-ammara) and the heart. He tested the servant with this and gathered these opposing forces within him, and He supplied each party with troops and helpers. The war therefore continues in turns and alternating victories between the two sides, until one of them overpowers the other and the other is subdued under it. When the turn belongs to the heart, the intellect and the angel, there is joy, bliss, pleasure, delight, happiness, the coolness of the eye, the goodness of life, the expansion of the chest, and the winning of spoils. When the turn belongs to the self, desire and Satan, there are griefs, cares, sorrows, all kinds of hardships, constriction of the chest, and the imprisonment of the king.

Consider, then, a king whose enemy has seized control over him, deposed him from his throne, taken him captive, imprisoned him, and placed between him and his treasures, his stores and his servants, and made them his own. Yet the king does not move to seek vengeance, does not call upon one who might aid him, and does not ask for help from anyone who might rescue him. Above this king is a King who cannot be subdued, a Victor who cannot be vanquished, and a Mighty One who cannot be humiliated. He sends to him: "If you seek help, I will help you; if you call upon Me for aid, I will aid you; if you turn to Me, I will avenge you; and if you flee to Me and take refuge with Me, I will give you authority over your enemy and place him under your control."

If the captive king says: "My enemy has tightened my bonds, fastened my restraints, secured me with chains, and prevented me from rising toward You, fleeing to You, and journeying to Your door. If You send troops from Your side to loosen my bonds, free my chains, and bring me out of his prison, I will be able to reach Your door; otherwise I cannot leave my prison or break my chains," and if he says this in protest against that sovereign, rejecting his message and content with what he is in at the hand of his enemy, then the Supreme Sultan will leave him as he is and entrust him to what he has chosen for himself.

But if he says this out of need for Him, in display of his own weakness and humiliation, acknowledging that he is too feeble and incapable to go to Him by himself, to exit the prison of his enemy, and to free himself by his own power and strength, and that it is part of the perfection of His favor upon him that, having sent this message to him, He should supply him from His troops and His slaves with someone to help him escape, break open the door of his prison, and unfasten his chains, then if He does this for him, He has completed His bounty upon him. And if He leaves him, He has not wronged him nor withheld from him anything that is rightfully his. Rather, His praiseworthiness and wisdom may require that He withhold help and leave him in his prison, especially when he knows that the prison is of His making, that this enemy who imprisoned him is a slave of His own, a servant of His servants, whose forelock is in His hand and who acts only by His permission and will. Such a captive is then neither attentive to the enemy, nor fearful of him, nor does he believe that the enemy has any share in the affair, or any power to benefit or harm. Rather, he looks only to his Master and the one who manages his affairs, the one whose forelock is in His hand. He has singled Him out with fear, hope, humble supplication, appeal, desire and awe. At that point the armies of victory and triumph come to him.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was never helped in any place as he was helped on the day of Uhud. When this was criticised against him, he said: 'Between me and whoever denies it stands the Book of Allah. Allah says: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾.'"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Al-hass (to kill)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions had the upper hand at the start of the day, until seven or nine of the polytheists had been killed." He then mentioned the hadith.

﴿Then He sent down upon you security, drowsiness overcoming a faction of you﴾. Allah sent drowsiness upon them as security from Him at the battles of Badr and Uhud. Drowsiness in battle and in times of fear is a sign of safety and comes from Allah, whereas drowsiness during prayer and in gatherings of remembrance and knowledge comes from Satan.

The angels fought on the day of Uhud on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), on the authority of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, and with him were two men fighting on his behalf, wearing white garments, fighting with the utmost ferocity. I had never seen them before, nor after."

In Sahih Muslim: "On the day of Uhud, he (ﷺ) was left alone with seven men from the Ansar and two men from Quraysh. When they pressed upon him, he said: 'Whoever repels them from us will have Paradise, or he will be my companion in Paradise.' A man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. Then they pressed upon him again, and he said: 'Whoever repels them from us will have Paradise, or he will be my companion in Paradise.' A man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. This continued until all seven were killed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We have not been fair to our Companions.'" This is narrated in two ways: with the fa' of ansafna pronounced with a sukun and ashabana in the accusative (naṣb) as the object, and with the fa' vowelled with a fatha and ashabuna in the nominative (raf') as the subject.

As for the accusative reading (ashabana, with naṣb): when the Ansar went out to fight one after another until they were killed, and the two Qurashi men did not come out, he said this, meaning: Quraysh were not fair to the Ansar.

As for the nominative reading (ashabuna, with raf'): the intended meaning of "the Companions" is those who fled from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until he was left with a small group, and they were killed one after another. Thus they were not fair to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or to those who stood firm with him.

In Sahih Ibn Hibban, on the authority of 'A'ishah, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "When the day of Uhud came, all the people turned away from the Prophet (ﷺ), and I was the first to return to the Prophet (ﷺ). I saw before him a man fighting on his behalf and defending him. I said: 'Be Talhah! May my father and mother be your ransom! Be Talhah! May my father and mother be your ransom!' Before long, Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah overtook me, running like a bird until he caught up with me. We advanced to the Prophet (ﷺ), and there was Talhah before him, prostrate and wounded. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Take your brother, for he has earned Paradise.' The Prophet (ﷺ) had been struck on his forehead, and his cheek was pierced, so that a ring of the helmet's links had sunk into his cheek. I went to pull it out from the Prophet (ﷺ), but Abu 'Ubaydah said: 'I adjure you by Allah, O Abu Bakr, to leave it to me!' So Abu 'Ubaydah took the arrowhead in his mouth and began to work it loose, lest he hurt the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he pulled the arrowhead out with his mouth, and one of Abu 'Ubaydah's front teeth fell out. Abu Bakr said: Then I went to pull out the other, and Abu 'Ubaydah said: 'I adjure you by Allah, O Abu Bakr, to leave it to me!' So he took it and began to work it loose until he pulled it out, and Abu 'Ubaydah's other front tooth fell out. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Take your brother, for he has earned Paradise.' We then turned to Talhah and treated him, and he had received about ten-odd blows."

In the Maghazi of al-Umawi: The polytheists climbed the mountain, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Sa'd: "Ajnibhum" (meaning: repel them). He said: "How can I repel them alone?" He said this three times. So Sa'd took an arrow from his quiver and shot a man, killing him. He said: "Then I took my arrow, recognised it, and shot another and killed him. Then I took it again, recognised it, and shot another and killed him. They then descended from their position." I said: "This is a blessed arrow," so I put it in my quiver, and it remained with Sa'd until he died, and then it remained with his sons.

In the Sahihayn, on the authority of Abu Hazim, who was asked about the wound of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "By Allah, I know who used to wash the wound of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and who used to pour the water, and with what it was treated. His daughter Fatimah used to wash it, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib used to pour the water with a shield. When Fatimah saw that the water only increased the bleeding, she took a piece of reed mat, burned it, and applied the ash, and the bleeding stopped."

In the Sahih: "His incisor (rubā'iyyah) was broken and his head was wounded. He began wiping the blood from him and saying: 'How can a people prosper who wounded the face of their prophet, and broke his tooth, while he calls them?' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿You have no say in the matter; He either turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 128]."

When the people were routed, Anas ibn al-Nadr did not flee. He said: "O Allah, I apologise to You for what these people have done (meaning the Muslims), and I disassociate myself before You from what these people have done (meaning the polytheists)." Then he advanced, and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh met him and said: "Where are you going, Abu 'Amr?" Anas said: "Wahan li-rīḥi al-jannah (how wonderful is the scent of Paradise), O Sa'd! I find it beyond Uhud." Then he went on, fought the enemy until he was killed. He was not recognised until his sister identified him by his fingertips. He had about eighty-odd wounds: stabs from spears, blows from swords, and arrow shots.

The polytheists were routed at the start of the day, as mentioned earlier. Then Iblis cried out among them: "O servants of Allah, may Allah disgrace you! Return from your retreat and fight."

Hudhayfah looked at his father while the Muslims were trying to kill him, thinking he was one of the polytheists. He said: "O servants of Allah! My father!" They did not understand his words until they had killed him. He said: "May Allah forgive you," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to pay his blood-money. He said: "I have given his blood-money as charity to the Muslims." This increased Hudhayfah's standing with the Prophet (ﷺ).

Zayd ibn Thabit said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me on the day of Uhud to search for Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'. He said to me: 'If you see him, convey my greetings to him and say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) says to you: How are you?'" He said: "I began walking among the dead until I reached him, and he was at his last breath, with seventy wounds: stabs from spears, blows from swords, and arrow shots. I said: 'O Sa'd, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sends you his greetings and says: Tell me how you are.' He said: 'And upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) be peace. Tell him: O Messenger of Allah, I smell the scent of Paradise. And tell my people, the Ansar: There is no excuse for you before Allah if harm reaches the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while there is an eye among you that blinks.'" And his soul departed at that very moment.

A man from the Muhajirun passed by a man from the Ansar who was writhing in his blood. He said: "O so-and-so, did you know that Muhammad has been killed?" The Ansari said: "If Muhammad has been killed, he has conveyed the message. So fight for your religion." Then this was revealed: ﴿Muhammad is not but a messenger; messengers have passed on before him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 144], and so on, the verse.

'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram said: "Before Uhud, I saw in a dream Mubashshir ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, who said to me: 'You will come to us in a few days.' I said: 'Where are you?' He said: 'In Paradise, where we roam freely wherever we wish.' I said to him: 'Were you not killed on the day of Badr?' He said: 'Yes, then I was brought back to life.' He mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: 'This is martyrdom, O Abu Jabir.'"

Khaythamah, the father of Sa'd, said, and his son had been martyred with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Badr: "The Battle of Badr passed me by, and by Allah, I was eager for it. Until I drew lots with my son for going out, and his lot came out, so he was granted martyrdom. Last night I saw my son in a dream in the most beautiful form, roaming among the fruits and rivers of Paradise, saying: 'Come to us, and you will accompany us in Paradise, for I have found what my Lord promised me to be true.' By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I have become longing to accompany him in Paradise. My age has advanced, my bones have become weak, and I love to meet my Lord. So pray to Allah, O Messenger of Allah, that He grant me martyrdom and companionship with Sa'd in Paradise." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed for him with that, and he was martyred at Uhud.

'Abdullah ibn Jahsh said on that day: "O Allah, I swear to You that tomorrow I will meet the enemy, and they will kill me, then slit my belly, cut off my nose and ears, and then You will ask me: 'Why did this happen to you?' and I will say: 'For You.'"

'Amr ibn al-Jamuh was severely lame, and he had four strong sons who used to go out to fight with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whenever he went on a campaign. When he set out for Uhud, he wanted to go with him, but his sons said to him: "Allah has granted you a dispensation. If you stay, we will take care of you, for Allah has lifted the obligation of jihad from you." 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these sons of mine prevent me from going out with you. By Allah, I hope to be martyred, and then I will step into Paradise with this lame leg of mine." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "As for you, Allah has lifted the obligation of jihad from you," and he said to his sons: "What harm is there if you let him go? Perhaps Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will grant him martyrdom." So he went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and was martyred on the day of Uhud.

(Anas ibn al-Nadr came upon 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah among men of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who had laid down their arms. He said: "What is keeping you here?" They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been killed." He said: "Then what will you do with life after him? Get up and die as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died." Then he faced the enemy and fought until he was killed.)

Ubayy ibn Khalaf, the enemy of Allah, came forward, fully armoured, saying: "I will not survive if Muhammad survives." He had sworn in Makkah that he would kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr confronted him, and Mus'ab was killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the collarbone (taraqwah) of Ubayy ibn Khalaf through a gap between the full coat of mail and the helmet, so he struck him with his spear. He fell from his horse, and his companions carried him away, while he was bellowing like a bull. They said: "Why are you so frightened? It is only a scratch." He told them what the Prophet (ﷺ) had said: "Rather, I will kill him, if Allah, Exalted, wills." And he died at Rabigh.

Ibn 'Umar said: "I was traveling through the valley of Rabigh late at night, when a fire blazed up for me. I approached it, and a man came out of it in chains, which he was dragging, crying out: 'Thirst!' And a man was saying: 'Do not give him drink, this is the slain one of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.'"

Nafi' ibn Jubayr said: "I heard a man from the Muhajirun say: 'I witnessed Uhud. I saw the arrows coming from every direction, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the middle of them, and all of them were turned away from him. I saw 'Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri that day saying: "Point me to Muhammad. May I not survive if he survives!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was beside him, with no one else with him. Then he passed him by, and Safwan rebuked him for this. He said: "By Allah, I did not see him. I swear by Allah, he was protected from us." So we went out, four of us, made a pact and agreed to kill him, but we could not reach him.'"

When Malik, the father of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, sucked the wound of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he cleaned it, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Spit it out." He said: "By Allah, I will never spit it out," and then he turned away. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wants to look at a man of the people of Paradise, let him look at this one."

(Admonition)

When someone who desires the world speaks with his words, every time he digs into a well his heart draws out, and he goes deep into derivation, the dust of greed collapses upon him and buries him.

When you see the cloak of this world has pulled away from you, know that it is a kindness to you. For the Benefactor has not withdrawn it out of stinginess, that it should tear; rather, out of gentleness toward the one who strives, lest he stumble.

[On the wisdom of the Battle of Uhud]

Section. Then Allah, glorified is He, informed of another wisdom in this decree: the testing of what is in their breasts (ibtila' ma fi sudurihim), that is, examining what is in them of faith and hypocrisy. The believer is not increased by this except in faith and submission, while the hypocrite, and the one in whose heart is a disease, must have what is in his heart appear upon his limbs and his tongue.

Then He mentioned another wisdom: the purification (tamhis) of what is in the hearts of the believers, meaning its clearing, cleansing and refining. The hearts are mixed with the dominance of natural dispositions, the inclination of souls, the rule of habit, the adornment of Satan, and the seizure of heedlessness, with what opposes what has been deposited in them of faith, Islam, righteousness and piety. Were they left in constant, uninterrupted well-being, they would not be cleared of this admixture nor purified of it. Therefore the wisdom of the Mighty decreed for them trials and tribulations that act as a bitter medicine for one who has contracted an illness, which, if his physician does not attend to it by removing and cleansing it from his body, would bring fear of corruption and destruction. Thus His blessing upon them through this breaking, defeat and the killing of those among them who were killed equals His blessing upon them through His help, support and their victory over their enemy. For Him is complete blessing upon them in this and in that.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, informed of the turning away of those among the sincere believers who turned away on that day, and that it was due to their earnings and their sins. Satan caused them to slip through those deeds until they turned away. Their deeds became an army against them, by which their enemy grew in strength. Indeed, deeds are an army for the servant and an army against him, without exception. For the servant, at every moment, there is a detachment from his own self that defeats him or supports him. He supplies his enemy with his deeds from a direction he thinks he is fighting with them, and sends to it a detachment that fights him alongside his enemy from a direction he thinks he is fighting his enemy. The servant's deeds drive him by compulsion toward their consequences of good and evil, and the servant either does not perceive this or perceives it and feigns blindness. So a person's flight from his enemy, while he is able to resist, is only by an army from his own deeds that Satan sent to him and through which he caused him to slip.

Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that He pardoned them, because this flight was not out of hypocrisy or doubt, but was a passing matter that Allah pardoned. Thus the courage of faith and its steadfastness returned to their place and their proper station.

Then Allah, glorified is He, repeated to them that what afflicted them came to them from their own selves and because of their deeds. He said: ﴿Why, when a disaster struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, did you say, "How is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent."﴾ [Al Imran: 165]. He mentioned this same matter in more general terms in the Meccan surahs, saying: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30], and He said: ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself.﴾ [An-Nisa: 79]. Here, the good and the evil are the blessing and the disaster: the blessing is from Allah, who bestowed it upon you as a favour, and the disaster arose only from your own self and your deeds. The first is His bounty, the second is His justice, and the servant moves between His bounty and His justice: His bounty flows over him, His judgement passes upon him, and His justice is the decree He issues.

He concluded the first verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ after His saying: ﴿Say, "It is from yourselves"﴾, informing them of the comprehensiveness of His power together with His justice, and that He is just and powerful. In this is the affirmation of divine decree (qadar) and of causation (sabab). He mentioned the cause and attributed it to their selves, and He mentioned the comprehensiveness of power and attributed it to Himself. The first negates compulsion (jabr), and the second negates the claim that decree is void. This resembles His saying: ﴿For whoever among you wills to take a straight path. And you do not will unless Allah wills, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [At-Takwir: 28-29].

In the mention of His power here there is a subtle point: this matter is in His hand and under His power, and He is the One who, had He willed, would have averted it from you. So do not seek the removal of its like from other than Him, and do not rely upon other than Him. He clarified this meaning and made it fully clear in His saying: ﴿And what afflicted you on the day the two armies met was by the permission of Allah﴾ [Al Imran: 166]. This is the permission that is cosmic and decreed (al-idhn al-kawni al-qadari), not the legislative, religious permission, like His saying concerning magic: ﴿And they could not harm anyone with it except by the permission of Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 102].

Then He informed of the wisdom of this decree, which is that He would make the believers distinguished from the hypocrites with a knowledge of direct observation and sight, by which one of the two groups is clearly distinguished from the other. Among the wisdom of this decree was that the hypocrites spoke what was in their souls, and the believers heard it, and they heard Allah's response to them and His answer to them. They knew the outcome of hypocrisy and where it leads, and how its bearer is deprived of the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, so that it returns upon him with the corruption of both this world and the Hereafter. So how many wisdoms there are, by Allah, within this story, sufficient and a complete blessing upon the believers, and how many warnings, intimidations, guidance, admonitions and explanations there are in it concerning the causes of good and evil, what each of them entails and their outcomes!

Then He consoled His Prophet and his allies concerning those among them who were killed in His cause, with the most excellent and gentlest consolation, the most effective in inviting them to be content with what He decreed for them.
